candidates.title: Civil Designer
candidates.abstract: Civil Designer role delivering high-quality design solutions on diverse infrastructure projects in Rockhampton.
candidates.content_text:
Job overview
If you’re a Civil Designer who enjoys owning your work and seeing projects through from concept to delivery, this is a great opportunity to step into a role with real responsibility. Based in our Rockhampton office, you’ll work on a mix of projects while being part of a close-knit team that values quality, accountability and practical outcomes. 
Rockhampton offers the best of both worlds. A relaxed regional lifestyle with easy access to the Capricorn Coast, plus the opportunity to work on diverse and impactful infrastructure projects across Queensland.
About the role
You’ll be responsible for producing civil designs and documentation that support project delivery from start to finish. Working closely with the General Manager, Project Managers and Senior Designers, your day-to-day will include designing, drafting and coordinating project information.
This is a hands-on role where you’ll:
- Prepare detailed design drawings, calculations and documentation
- Use tools like 12d and AutoCAD to deliver accurate, compliant designs
- Liaise with councils, authorities and external stakeholders
- Manage and maintain project documentation and drawing registers
- Support project timelines by working efficiently and flagging risks early
- Provide guidance to Cadet Designers and Drafters within the team
You’ll be trusted to manage your workload, contribute to project outcomes and take pride in the quality of your deliverables.
What we’re looking for
What you’ll need:
- Around 3+ years’ experience in civil design/drafting
- Practical experience using AutoCAD and 12d Model
- Strong understanding of engineering design principles, standards and approvals processes
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines
- High attention to detail and a sense of ownership over your work 
Nice to have:
- An associate degree in Civil Engineering or similar
- Experience liaising with local councils or state authorities
Just as important as your technical skills is your ability to work well with others, communicate clearly and stay proactive when challenges arise.
The team and environment 
You’ll be joining a supportive, down-to-earth team where people pull together and get things done. It’s a professional office environment without the layers of bureaucracy. You’ll have direct access to decision-makers and the opportunity to contribute ideas.
There’s also a strong focus on mentoring and development, particularly with junior designers, so your willingness to share knowledge will be valued.
Why Join
- Work on a variety of civil projects with real impact
- Be part of a stable, growing business with an established reputation
- Enjoy a regional lifestyle in Rockhampton, close to the coast and outdoor lifestyle opportunities
- Genuine opportunity to develop your skills and take on more responsibility
- Flexible, supportive working environment that values accountability over micromanagement
- Additional day of leave on your birthday
- Annual Wellness Benefit to use towards healthy lifestyle initiatives 
- Grow our team with our generous referral bonus
candidates.teaser: Civil Designer role delivering high-quality design solutions on diverse infrastructure projects in Rockhampton.

candidates.title: Project Engineer - Civil Construction
candidates.abstract: Join a major Western Sydney civil infrastructure project delivering earthworks, roads and utilities. Strong pipeline and genuine career growth.
candidates.content_text:
Project Engineer – Civil Infrastructure Western Sydney (near Western Sydney Airport) | Immediate Start
 Join a major civil infrastructure project helping deliver critical works within one of Australia's fastest-growing development corridors.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 We are seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the delivery of a large-scale civil infrastructure project involving bulk earthworks, utilities, roads, drainage and associated subdivision works.
 Working closely with the Project Manager and site delivery team, you will play a key role in coordinating subcontractors, managing consultant and design interfaces, resolving technical queries and ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
 The role will involve significant coordination between site teams, subcontractors, design consultants and external stakeholders to ensure design documentation, approvals and construction activities remain aligned with the project programme.
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing contractor with a strong pipeline of work across Western Sydney.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Coordinate day-to-day project delivery activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Manage subcontractors, suppliers, consultants and design interfaces.
 - Coordinate with civil, structural, services and other design consultants to resolve technical and construction-related issues.
 - Manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design clarifications, ensuring timely responses from relevant consultants.
 - Support design management activities, including design reviews, documentation coordination, constructability assessments and design changes.
 - Monitor design deliverables, approvals and outstanding information to ensure construction activities remain on programme.
 - Prepare and manage RFIs, NCRs, ITPs, SWMS reviews and project documentation.
 - Monitor programme, productivity and project milestones.
 - Assist with procurement, scope packages and subcontractor management.
 - Track project costs, variations and progress claims.
 - Support quality assurance and compliance activities across site.
 - Liaise with client representatives, authorities and key project stakeholders.
 - Prepare regular project reporting and progress updates.
 - Drive efficient project outcomes through proactive problem solving and coordination.
 SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
 - Experience as a Project Engineer within civil infrastructure, subdivisions or earthworks projects.
 - Strong understanding of bulk earthworks, roads, drainage and utility installation.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering consultants and managing design-related issues during construction.
 - Ability to manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design documentation.
 - Experience reviewing construction drawings, identifying design discrepancies and coordinating practical solutions.
 - Strong subcontractor management, project documentation and stakeholder coordination skills.
 - Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple work fronts in a live construction environment.
 - Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 - Proficient with project management and reporting systems such as Procore, Laminar or similar.
 - Relevant Civil Engineering qualification.
 THE OPPORTUNITY
 - Major infrastructure project within the Western Sydney Airport growth corridor.
 - Long-term project pipeline and strong job security.
 - Exposure to large-scale civil infrastructure and subdivision works.
 - Broad involvement across engineering, design coordination and construction delivery.
 - High-performing and collaborative project team.
 - Genuine career progression opportunities.
 THE DETAILS
 - Full-time, site-based position.
 - Western Sydney location.
 - Competitive salary package based on experience.
 - Immediate start available.
 HOW TO APPLY
 Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

There is an opportunity for a Civil Engineering Draftsperson / CAD Draftsperson to join MJB Industries Pty Ltd, a fast-paced Australian owned company led by passionate hands-on directors.
MJB Industries Pty Ltd is one of Western Australia’s biggest manufacturers of precast concrete products and concrete pipe. MJB have an opportunity available for a confident, collaborative, and technically minded candidate to fulfill the role of Civil Engineering Draftsperson / CAD Draftsmen. A minimum of 1 year proven experience in a similar role is required with extensive knowledge and experience using drafting and modeling software (AutoCAD 2D & 3D).
The ideal candidate will have a high attention to detail, positive attitude, be willing to get hands on with a variety of projects and have excellent time management skills. candidates.content_text:
Location: Rockhampton
Remuneration/Benefit: Competitive remuneration including overtime. Relocation packages available.
About the role:
Aurizon Network Asset Management is looking for a motivated Civil / Structural Engineer to join our Civil and Structures Assets team and help shape the future of one of Australia’s most important rail networks.
You will contribute to the asset management strategy that connects inland producers with ports along the Queensland coast, from Bowen through Sarina to Gladstone. This is a broad, hands-on role offering exposure to the full asset lifecycle—from understanding asset condition and risk through to shaping renewal scopes, budgets, designs and delivery priorities.
You will help develop capital renewal and maintenance programs across a diverse civil and structures portfolio, including:
- Structures — more than 4,000 culverts, 300 bridges, retaining walls and other structural assets
- Level crossings — more than 700 crossings with a mix of active and passive controls
- Geotechnical and earthworks — steep slopes through several mountain ranges and the formation supporting the track asset
- Access points and access roads — connecting our teams safely and efficiently with railway infrastructure
- Corridor security and fencing — supporting a rail network across an area larger than Tasmania
Working closely with Design Management, Program Management, operations and maintenance teams, you will influence practical, whole-of-business outcomes from concept and design through to delivery of renewal works—balancing safety, risk, track access, cost and scope.
- Influence stakeholders across the business to achieve better outcomes for civil and structures assets
- Assess asset condition, defects and failure modes, applying risk-based engineering judgement to support investment decisions
- Develop renewal and maintenance scopes, budgets and forward programs, and manage changes through planning and delivery
- Improve the processes, tools and data used to make asset management decisions
- Develop and refine strategies, standards, policies and practical engineering guidelines
- Analyse asset information and translate it into clear priorities and recommendations
Around 20% of your time will be spent in the field travelling across the network, giving you direct exposure to the assets you manage and the people who operate and maintain them. The balance offers flexible working across the office and home.
About you:
You are an early-to-mid career Civil or Structural Engineer who is ready to broaden your experience beyond a single project or discipline. You bring experience in design, construction and/or asset management, and you are keen to apply your technical knowledge in a practical operational environment. You enjoy solving complex problems, learning from experienced professionals and working with a wide range of stakeholders to turn sound engineering into real-world outcomes.
Qualifications and experience:
- Bachelor of Civil Engineering or equivalent (mandatory)
- Approximately 2–8 years’ experience in a civil or structural engineering role (mandatory)
- The ability to obtain registration a Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ) in the next 2 years (preferred)
- Experience with rail track infrastructure (desirable, but not essential)
What you will bring:
- A practical understanding of infrastructure operations, design, construction, maintenance and safety requirements
- Clear communication skills and the confidence to consult, negotiate and influence at different levels of the business
- The ability to apply legislation, regulation, standards and engineering requirements in a practical and proportionate way
- Strong written communication skills, with an interest in developing standards, specifications, policies, guidelines and processes
- Commercial awareness and the ability to balance risk, performance, cost and deliverability
If you are ready to accelerate your development, take ownership of a diverse infrastructure portfolio and see the impact of your decisions in the field, we would like to hear from you.
What we offer you:             
At Aurizon, we support the development and growth of our employees. With a national portfolio of operations, we offer long-term and exciting career opportunities. 
Some of our benefits include:
- Development and growth opportunities.
- Access to mentoring and development programs.
- Discounts on selected health insurance funds, personal travel, gyms, vehicles and retail brands.
- Parental leave program and super booster.
About Aurizon.
Aurizon is Australia’s largest rail freight operator and a top 100 ASX company. Each year, we deliver more than 250 million tonnes of Australian commodities right across the country. Aurizon is crucial to the Australian economy, connecting miners, primary producers and industry with international and domestic markets. 
Look to Aurizon for a diverse and collaborative culture.
At Aurizon, we are proud of our diverse, collaborative, creative and high-performance culture. We celebrate the contribution of every employee and provide opportunities for career development in a dynamic, caring, and inclusive work environment.
To learn about us and our company values, please visit www.aurizon.com.au/careers

candidates.content_text:
About Smart Built
Smart Built Pty. Ltd. is an Adelaide-based domestic and commercial building contractor providing Package Solutions, Head Contracting and Project Management services.
We deliver a range of residential and commercial projects, including stand-alone and multi-unit developments, commercial buildings, renovations and extensions. Our team works closely with architects, engineers, consultants, subcontractors and suppliers from the design and approval stages through to construction.
About the role
We are seeking a qualified and proactive Civil Engineer to join our team to plan, design, coordinate and oversee civil works for residential and commercial construction projects.
Working closely with our project team and external consultants, you will exercise professional engineering judgement, develop and review civil engineering solutions, coordinate design and construction requirements, and resolve technical issues throughout the project lifecycle.
Role Responsibilities
·       Plan and design civil works for residential and commercial developments, including site levels, earthworks, stormwater drainage, pavements, retaining works and associated water and sewer infrastructure, and prepare and verify the related engineering calculations, drawings and technical specifications.
·       Determine appropriate construction methods, materials and quality standards, and prepare, review and interpret engineering drawings, plans, specifications and construction procedures.
·       Coordinate and oversee construction activities, including site preparation, earthworks, drainage, concrete and associated civil works, and organise site labour and the delivery of materials, plant and equipment to support efficient project delivery.
·       Analyse site conditions and geotechnical reports to determine design parameters for earthworks, drainage, foundations and retaining works, and coordinate specialist investigations or testing where required.
·       Undertake and verify engineering calculations and technical assessments to develop, optimise and confirm the performance and constructability of civil works and associated building components.
·       Review architectural, structural and civil engineering drawings and specifications to assess constructability and engineering requirements, and provide technical input into quantity take-offs, cost estimates and budget control.
·       Assess proposed design changes and construction variations for their engineering, constructability, compliance, program and cost impacts, and prepare technical recommendations to support variation management.
·       Liaise with architects, engineers, consultants, contractors, subcontractors and suppliers to resolve design and construction issues and ensure civil works are delivered in accordance with approved designs and specifications.
·       Inspect and oversee civil construction works, monitor progress, quality and conformance with approved designs, identify technical issues and defects, and develop or recommend appropriate engineering solutions.
·       Prepare engineering calculations, design documentation, technical reports and site inspection records, respond to technical queries, and ensure civil works comply with relevant legislation, Australian Standards, WHS requirements and company procedures.
Requirements
·       Bachelor's degree or higher qualification in Civil Engineering.
·       At least five years of post-qualification professional civil engineering experience, preferably in residential or commercial development.
·       Strong knowledge of civil engineering principles, construction methods, materials, Australian Standards and site practices
·       Experience interpreting engineering drawings, technical specifications and construction documentation
·       Demonstrated experience in planning and designing civil works, including drainage, earthworks, site levels and foundations, for residential and commercial developments
·       Strong analytical, problem-solving and project coordination skills
·       Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
·       Proficiency in AutoCAD, Microsoft Office and relevant engineering, estimating or project management software
·       Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality, safety and compliance
·       Ability to work effectively in office and construction site environments

The Preservation and Maintenance team delivers maintenance, rehabilitation and road safety projects, while the Asset Management team assesses road condition and plans future works.  Principal Engineer (PO5)

 - Supervise, allocate and mentor engineering and technical staff

 Senior Civil Engineer (PO4)

 - Assess construction tenders, manage procurement and administer complex contracts

 - Supervise and mentor engineers, graduates and technical staff

 - Calculate material quantities, review test results and manage non-conformances

 - Willing to undergo a criminal history check (essential, all roles)
 Preferred Qualifications

Parklife Metro JV is leading the delivery of the Sydney Metro - Western Sydney Airport project, a landmark transport initiative that will link St Marys to Bradfield and seamlessly connect with the new Western Sydney Airport.
This visionary project driven by a joint venture between Plenary, RATP Dev, Siemens, and Webuild includes the construction of six new stations, 12 state-of-the-art metro trains, advanced rail systems, and a modern stabling and maintenance facility at Orchard Hills.
As the largest public-private partnership (PPP) ever awarded in New South Wales, this $5 billion project is set to redefine the future of Greater Western Sydney by enhancing connectivity and driving economic growth. Being part of Parklife Metro JV means joining a transformative infrastructure venture with the chance to grow your career in a fast-paced, forward-thinking environment.
This is more than just a rail project. It's a critical step in shaping the long-term social and economic fabric of Western Sydney. The infrastructure being delivered will support the region's expected population growth, improve access to employment hubs, and promote sustainable, integrated urban development. At the heart of this transformation is a commitment to innovation, sustainability, and community impact.
Parklife Metro JV is building a culture that values collaboration, diversity, and inclusion. With a strong focus on safety, professional development, and creating lasting benefits for local communities, our team is empowered to push boundaries and deliver excellence at every stage. Whether you're an engineer, project manager, systems specialist, or corporate professional, you'll be part of a high-performing team working on one of the most significant infrastructure projects in Australia's history.
Benefits:
 - Competitive remuneration package
 - Diversity & inclusion initiatives
 - Employee recognition programs
 - Growth and development opportunities within a large-scale project
 - Health & wellbeing initiatives
 - Novated leases
 - Supportive and collaborative work culture
 - Work on one of the most exciting infrastructure projects in Australia
The Opportunity:
Employed by Webuild, Parklife Metro is seeking an Undergraduate Engineer to join our Design & Engineering - Interface & SESA team based in Sydney CBD. 
As an Undergraduate Engineer, you will gain exposure to the design coordination, requirements management and assurance functions of a major rail infrasturtucre project while contributing to defined SESASI (Systems Engineering, Safety Assurance & Systems Integration) deliverables alongside our experienced team. 
Duties & Responsibilities:
 - Support requirements traceability activities, including correlation of design and construction requirements within the Requirements Verification and Traceability Matrix (RVTM).
 - Attend design coordination, interface and assurance meetings in an observation and note-taking capacity, and prepare draft minutes for review.
 - Support the preparation of evidence packs for assurance submissions, including document reference checking and completeness verification.
 - Undertake structured review of civil design documentation to build familiarity with drawing sets, specifications and design reports.
 - Prepare short written summaries and data extracts to support the Engineering Manager's reporting obligations.
 - Complete all mandatory inductions and comply with project WHS, confidentiality and information handling requirements.
 Criteria:
 - Currently studying a degree in Civil Engineering or similar
 - Adaptable and collaborative team player 
 - Willingness to learn and thrive 
What's Next?
If you're ready to take the next step in your career within one of Australia's largest infrastructure projects, we encourage you to submit your CV by clicking ‘Apply'.
Interested in learning more about Parklife Metro JV or Webuild? Visit our websites at https://parklifemetro.com.au & Webuild S.p.A. Jobs.
Join us and help deliver a legacy that will serve generations to come while building a rewarding and purpose-driven career.

candidates.content_text:
An opportunity for a Site Engineer - Services Infrastructure to build experience on a major Defence program at Blamey Barracks Kapooka, supporting the delivery of HV, water, fire and sewer infrastructure packages.
The Riverina Redevelopment Joint Venture (RRJV) is a 50/50 joint venture between CPB Contractors and Downer to undertake major upgrades and replacement of existing infrastructure and facilities to support Defence capability for the next 30 years.
The proposed project consists of a program of works across three Department of Defence establishments including:
- Albury Wodonga Military Area (including North, South & East Bandiana, Latchford Barracks, Wirlinga)
- Blamey Barracks (Kapooka)
- RAAF Base Wagga
The proposed capital investment of $2 billion will incorporate a variety of elements including:
- Construction of new messing and living in accommodation
- Construction of new training facilities
- Refurbishment and upgrading of existing buildings
- Remedial works and upgrades to infrastructure services
To review all Downer opportunities on the Riverina Deployment Joint Venture (RRJV) please visit the website: Downer in the NSW Riverina - Downer Group Australia
The opportunity
We are seeking a Site Engineer - Services Infrastructure to support the delivery of critical Defence services works at Blamey Barracks Kapooka. Working closely with the Project Engineer, this role will assist in managing the installation of key services infrastructure packages, ensuring works are delivered safely, to quality standards and in line with RRJV systems. This is an excellent opportunity for a developing engineer to gain experience on a tier 1 Defence infrastructure program.
What you'll do
- Support the Project Engineer with the delivery of services infrastructure works including HV electrical, potable water, fire water and sewer mains
- Coordinate subcontractors to ensure works are delivered safely on program and to specification
- Assist with resolving design and constructability issues on site
- Support quality control activities, inspections and documentation
- Assist with commissioning and handover activities for completed services packages
What you'll bring
- Degree qualification in Services Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, Hydraulic or Building Services) or Civil Engineering
- Exposure to services infrastructure installations in a site or graduate engineering role
- Understanding of subcontractor coordination and site-quality processes
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work within a multidisciplinary project team
- Experience on construction or infrastructure projects (Defence experience advantageous but not essential)
This role is based at Wagga Wagga. Relocation assistance is available for the successful candidate if required. This is not a DIDO or FIFO role, applicants must be willing to relocate, be an Australian citizen and willing to obtain a security clearance.
Spotless Management Services Pty Ltd (a Downer Company) is delivering the works as part of a joint venture with CPB Contractors Pty Ltd. Accordingly we will share your Personal Information, to the extent necessary, for the purpose of recruitment for the joint venture with CPB Contractors Pty Ltd who are required to handle that information in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). 
Why Downer?
At Downer, we plan, create, and sustain essential public services across Australia and New Zealand. From hospitals to data centres and defence partnerships, we manage critical infrastructure that keeps communities thriving.
What It Means to Belong at Downer
We're proud of our high-performance culture and commitment to diversity, offering:
- Training and development to support and diversify your career.
- With 30% of vacancies filled internally you'll find real opportunities to advance your career.
- Perks@Downer: healthcare discounts, great savings on retail purchases, car purchases and much more.
- Employee Assistance Program: professional support for you and your family when you need it most.
You want your work to matter and so do we. With over 26,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific, our team is made up of individuals with unique perspectives, backgrounds, and ideas.
We know that diversity makes us stronger and we actively celebrate it through our commitment to inclusion and belonging.
We're committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities we serve and we welcome people of all ages, genders, sexual orientations, cultures, abilities, and lived experiences. We especially encourage applications from those whose voices have traditionally been underrepresented in our industry, including women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, Māori and Pasifika Peoples, veterans, people with disability, and neurodivergent individuals. Even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with this role, we'd still like to hear from you. If it feels like the right fit, apply - potential counts, and so do you.
As a WORK180 Endorsed Employer, we support flexibility that works for your life, inclusive leadership that values your voice, and equitable access to opportunity so you can do your best work and bring your whole self to it.
If you need support or adjustments through the recruitment process, just let us know, we're here to help you put your best foot forward.

candidates.content_text:
Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.
You’ve built your technical skills. You’re ready to take on more responsibility, contribute your ideas and develop the confidence to lead.
Rain Consulting is looking for a Project Engineer or Scientist with 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience to join our Melbourne team.
We’re a specialist stormwater and surface water consultancy. We plan and design better water environments, investigate how water behaves and help clients turn complex information into decisions they can act on.
Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.
And behind each challenge, there are people who need help turning complex information into a clear way forward.
These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.
We want you to question assumptions and contribute ideas. If you see a better way to approach a problem, explain a result or manage water, there’s room to explore it with us.
As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.
We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences.

candidates.content_text:
Works Engineer
Merriwa
Permanent Full-Time – (35 hours per week)  
The role:
Council is seeking an experienced and motivated Works Engineer to help deliver vital infrastructure and services across the Merriwa area. This is a diverse and rewarding role where you will play a key part in planning, managing and delivering Council’s construction and maintenance programs that support our communities.
Working within the Works Delivery team, you will oversee Council’s construction and maintenance activities across roads, bridges, footpaths, drainage, parks and facilities, as well as supporting the management of Council’s quarries. You will provide technical guidance, coordinate resources and contractors, and ensure projects and maintenance works are delivered safely, efficiently, within budget and to a high standard.
The role also provides an opportunity to work closely with Transport for NSW, including supporting Council’s compliance under the Roads Maintenance Council Contract (RMCC), as well as contributing to grant funding submissions, capital works programs and strategic infrastructure planning.
This is a great opportunity to contribute to meaningful infrastructure projects while enjoying the lifestyle of the beautiful Upper Hunter region and being part of a supportive and dedicated Council team.
What’s on offer:
- A competitive salary package (minimum offer of $111k + 12% super) can be negotiated with the preferred applicant.
- Four weeks of Annual Leave per year.
- Access to Rental & Relocation Policies.
- Generous uniform allowance.
- Access to Long Service Leave after five years.
- Training and upskilling opportunities.
- Salary sacrifice options.
About you:
You are an experienced and practical engineering professional who enjoys working collaboratively to deliver high-quality infrastructure and services for the community. You thrive in a dynamic environment where no two days are the same – coordinating works, managing contractors, supporting operational teams, solving problems and ensuring projects and maintenance activities are delivered safely, efficiently and within budget.
With a strong understanding of civil construction and maintenance operations, you provide technical guidance and leadership across roads, drainage, parks, facilities and other infrastructure. You lead by example, promote safe work practices, and take pride in delivering outcomes that enhance community infrastructure and public spaces.
Your application will further demonstrate:
- Tertiary qualifications in Engineering (Civil or related discipline) plus relevant experience in a similar role.
- Demonstrated experience implementing and promoting Work Health and Safety requirements.
- Experience coordinating minor works, capital projects and maintenance activities/schedules.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Demonstrated experience managing contractors and day labour teams to effectively deliver works and services.
About us:
Council is a progressive and caring organisation where all our employees work together to deliver quality services to support our community. We strive to make a difference and add value to the lives of our community. Everything we do is underpinned by the values of the organisation and staff, which are being honest, open and accountable, having mutual respect for all people and cultures, ensuring we deliver on our commitments, providing efficient, effective and reliable services to ensure staff and community safety and to provide improved environmental responsibility.
Located in the picturesque Upper Hunter, our shire encompasses the townships of Merriwa, Murrurundi, Aberdeen and Scone. All great places to live and work, come and see for yourself!

Wednesday 28 October 2026

We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and value diversity and inclusion in our workplace. We encourage all applicants, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disability, LGBTIQ and culturally diverse communities to join Council.
Council will provide reasonable adjustments for individuals with disability throughout the recruitment process. You'll organise your own workload, follow up outstanding items and make sure jobs keep moving.
For the right person, there is a genuine opportunity to grow into a Project Management / Operations role as the business grows.
WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:
- Attending site to take accurate measurements and identify practical installation issues
- Understanding and explaining to clients and crews how the work will be installed
- Leading and coordinating installations when required, working alongside the crew and being prepared to assist hands-on where appropriately trained and competent
- Preparing AutoCAD 2D drawings and site layouts for A-Class and B-Class hoardings and temporary structures
- Preparing workshop drawings showing what needs to be made, including measurements, materials and cutting lengths where required
- Reading and interpreting architectural, structural, civil and survey drawings
- Preparing material and labour take-offs
- Estimating labour, steel, timber, transport, crane/HIAB, EWP, engineering, installation and dismantle
- Obtaining prices from suppliers and subcontractors when needed
- Preparing quotations and detailed scopes of work
- Preparing drawings to meet SafeWork NSW Codes of Practice, Australian Standards and council requirements, including clearances, pedestrian protection, access and structural arrangements
- Supporting council submissions and reviewing the specific requirements of different NSW councils, including City of Sydney Type-A and Type-B hoarding requirements
- Managing multiple projects, following up outstanding items and keeping jobs moving from enquiry to installation
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:
Essential
- Practical, hands-on site experience: you can take accurate measurements, identify installation issues, and understand and explain how the work will be installed
- Hands-on leadership and practical site capability: able to confidently run or coordinate an installation, understand the work being carried out, and lead by example when required
- Strong AutoCAD 2D drafting skills
- Ability to use SolidWorks or similar 3D software (you don't need to be an expert in 3D modelling)
- Ability to prepare workshop drawings for fabrication, including measurements, materials and cutting lengths
- Estimating experience, including obtaining supplier and subcontractor pricing
- Solid understanding of structural steel, beams, posts, baseplates, bracing, timber framing, plywood, gates and connections
- Strong initiative and ownership: able to organise your workload, follow up outstanding items and keep jobs moving without constant direction
- Strong attention to detail
- Confidence dealing directly with builders, project managers, engineers and site supervisors
- Knowledge of, or the ability to quickly get across, the SafeWork NSW Overhead Protective Structures Code of Practice (commenced 12 December 2025), relevant Australian Standards and council requirements
- Good Excel skills
- Current driver licence
Preferred
- Ideally 5+ years of relevant experience in structural steel, scaffolding, temporary works, hoardings, façade, architectural metalwork or similar construction
- NSW construction experience
Please note: This role is not suited to someone who has only worked behind a desk producing drawings. We need someone who is comfortable on site and understands how the job actually gets built.
WHAT WE OFFER
- An opportunity to grow into a Project Management / Operations role as the business grows
- Ownership of projects from start to finish
- Varied work across commercial, residential and mixed-use developments in Sydney and NSW
- A growing business where initiative is noticed and rewarded
- [Salary/vehicle / other benefits TBD]

Join Orange City Council as the Engineering Design Coordinator and lead the design behind infrastructure that supports a growing regional city. This is an opportunity to combine your civil engineering expertise, leadership skills and practical problem-solving to deliver lasting outcomes for the Orange community.
Why join Orange City Council?
 - Work Life Balance – We offer flexible working arrangements, hybrid working, and generous leave provisions

 - Career – Opportunity to grow and develop with excellent learning and development opportunities

 - Competitive salary – $104,770 to $114,199 plus superannuation
About the role
As Engineering Design Coordinator, you will guide the delivery of high-quality, practical and cost-effective engineering designs for Council infrastructure projects. You will lead the Design team, coordinate consultants, provide trusted technical and strategic advice, and work constructively with developers, colleagues and the community. From concept and investigation through to approvals and construction standards, you will help turn complex engineering challenges into solutions that serve Orange now and into the future.

 - Lead and support the Design team, creating a clear sense of purpose and encouraging strong performance
 - Manage the delivery of engineering designs in line with Australian Standards, Council’s Development and Subdivision Code, and Transport for NSW requirements
 - Coordinate design consultants to deliver practical, timely and cost-effective outcomes
 - Provide strategic technical advice, engineering computations, estimates and contract specifications across roads, stormwater, water, sewerage, parks and other infrastructure
 - Work with developers and assist with the assessment and approval of engineering plans
 - Investigate and report on infrastructure, drainage, flooding and traffic matters
 - Manage inspections, construction standards, compliance, risk and work health and safety requirements
What you’ll bring
 - A degree qualification in Civil Engineering or another relevant discipline
 - Extensive experience in engineering design
 - Knowledge of stormwater modelling and the ability to interpret relevant legislation, standards and technical requirements
 - Proven leadership and supervisory capability, with an ability to coach, mentor and develop others
 - Strong communication and relationship-management skills across consultants, developers, colleagues and the community
 - Strategic thinking, sound judgement and a practical, creative approach to solving complex problems
 - Excellent planning and organisational skills, supported by strong digital capability
 - A current Class C driver licence
Read the full Position Description to learn more about the role (link available on Council’s website)
Keen to Learn More? 
 - Visit www.orange.nsw.gov.au to discover more about Orange City Council

Apply by submitting your resume and providing a brief response as to why you are a great fit for this role! Applications close Wednesday 28 October 2026.

At Regal Innovations, we are proud of our legacy of success and growth. Our experienced, highly skilled teams are empowered to make decisions, reflecting our agility and commitment to adapting to our clients' needs. With a focus on excellence and innovation, we continue to deliver outstanding results across Australia.
What’s On Offer?
- Company phone, laptop, and a full kit of uniform.
- Build your career through professional development and progression.
- Predictable Monday - Friday work schedule.
- A supportive and collaborative team environment.
Regal is looking for a highly organised Project Coordinator to provide critical support to our project and site teams, helping to deliver high-quality civil construction projects. The expected salary for this role is $85,000 - $110,000 per annum plus superannuation.
In this role, you will be the central point of coordinator for project admin, procurement, documentation, and communication. You will work alongside Project Managers, Site Managers, suppliers, subcontractors and more. 
Key Responsibilities
As a Project Coordinator, you will be responsible for:
- Providing day-to-day administrative and coordination support to Project and Site Managers.
- Preparing, distribute, and maintain project documentation, including drawings, purchase orders, subcontractor records, and variations.
- Coordinating staff, subcontractors, deliveries, equipment, and site meetings.
- Monitoring project progress and assist with milestone reporting.
- Liaise with suppliers to coordinate materials and delivery schedules.
- Preparing purchase orders, obtain supplier and subcontractor quotations, and assist with procurement activities.
- Supporting cost tracking, progress claims, subcontractor payments, and project variations.
- Assisting with maintaining WHS, Quality, and Environmental compliance documentation, including SWMS, inspections, and safety records.
- Acting as the key administrative link between site teams and head office while fostering strong relationships with clients, suppliers, and subcontractors.
- Contributing to the continuous improvement of project administration systems and processes.
Skills & Experience
- Qualifications in Business Administration, Construction Management, or a related discipline.
- A current Driver’s Licence and Construction White Card.
- Proven experience in project administration or site coordination, specifically within construction, civil, landscaping or a related industry.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent time management and attention to detail.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and comfortable using project management software (e.g. MS Projects).
- You are proactive, adaptable, and thrive in fast-paced environments.
About Regal Innovations
For fifty years, Regal Innovations has been transforming Australia's public spaces, turning ordinary parks, streets, and civic grounds into places people actually want to be. What began as a landscaping business has grown into an award-winning company trusted by governments, developers, and urban planners to deliver civil works, infrastructure, commercial and heritage projects across the country, with innovation at the heart of every project.
Questions?
We aim to process applications within a timely matter. If you have any questions regarding the role you applied for or your application, please contact careers@regalinnovations.com.au. 
As an equal opportunity employer, Regal is committed to a recruitment process that's fair, inclusive, free from bias, and accessible to everyone. By bringing together diverse backgrounds and perspectives, we support positive collective growth and development toward excellence.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are encouraged to apply.
candidates.teaser: Drive project success by coordinating teams, procurement and documentation , keeping civil construction projects organised, efficient and on track.

candidates.title: Construction & Engineering Adjuster | Career Transition Opportunity | Bonus+Car
candidates.abstract: Build a specialist Construction & Engineering claims career with training and mentoring. No previous loss adjusting experience required.
bullets: No loss adjusting experience needed - expert training and support provided
Competitive salary, annual performance bonus and car allowance
Structured career progression, ongoing training and professional development
candidates.content_text:
Turn your property, insurance, construction, engineering or project management experience into a specialist career in Construction & Engineering loss adjusting. No previous loss adjusting experience is required. At Crawford, you'll receive training, mentoring and support from experienced specialists as you develop your skills and manage increasingly complex commercial claims.
Why Join Crawford?
 - Rewarding package - Competitive salary, annual performance bonus, car allowance, laptop and phone 
 - Specialist career path - Build expertise in Construction & Engineering loss adjusting 
 - Professional development - Ongoing training, mentoring and industry qualifications 
 - Interesting work - Manage commercial construction and engineering claims across a wide range of industries 
 - Supportive team - Learn from experienced Construction, Engineering and Major Loss specialists 
What You Will Do
 - Investigate and manage Construction & Engineering claims from assessment through to settlement 
 - Review policies, contracts and claim documentation to determine coverage 
 - Prepare reports and claim recommendations for insurers and stakeholders 
 - Liaise with policyholders, brokers, contractors and technical experts 
 - Maintain strong client service standards and claim outcomes 
 - Assist with client meetings and business development activities as your experience grows 
What You Will Bring
You may currently be working in insurance claims, loss adjusting, construction, engineering, quantity surveying, project management or a related technical environment and be looking to specialise further. 
You will bring:
 - Property, construction, engineering or insurance claims experience 
 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills 
 - Analytical thinking and sound decision-making ability 
 - Strong organisation and time management skills 
 - A desire to build a long-term career in specialist loss adjusting 
 - Insurance, construction, engineering or related qualifications (desirable) 
 - Current Driver's Licence
About Crawford
Crawford is the world's largest publicly listed claims management company, supporting insurers, brokers, businesses and communities across more than 70 countries. 
Ready to Build Your Specialist Career?
If you're looking to combine your property, insurance, construction or engineering experience with a rewarding long-term career path, we'd love to hear from you.
Submit your resume and tell us why this opportunity is right for you.

candidates.title: Access Engineer
candidates.abstract: This role offers a mix of office-based work, project engagement & occasional site visits, great for someone who enjoys variety & working with people!
bullets: Build experience across projects, operations and engineering teams.
Fixed-term opportunity through to June 2029!
Hybrid working model and free Myki travel across Victoria.
candidates.content_text:
Access Engineer
·         Build experience across projects, operations and engineering teams.
·         Fixed-term opportunity through to June 2029!
·         Hybrid working model and free Myki travel across Victoria.
V/Line’s purpose is to connect Victorians through safe, reliable, and accessible transport. We believe in giving all Victorians opportunities through travel and transport – connecting them to jobs, education, family and friends, services, tourism and trade.
V/Line is experiencing significant growth and we’re delivering more services, more trains, cheaper fares, and huge projects. With more than 3700 weekly train and coach services, an expansive freight network and unprecedented rail investment, millions of Victorians depend on us to deliver. You could be one of our 3100 committed team members who are up to the challenge.
About the role
Reporting to the Projects Access Interface Team Leader, the Access Engineer is responsible for assessing requests from third parties seeking access to the V/Line network. You'll review access applications, provide advice on safety and operational requirements, coordinate with stakeholders across the business and support the delivery of projects in a safe, compliant and efficient manner.
Key accountabilities include:
·         Assess and respond to third-party access applications across the V/Line network.
·         Review proposed works and provide advice on safety, operational and environmental requirements.
·         Issue Site Access Permits and maintain accurate application records.
·         Work closely with project teams, contractors and internal stakeholders to support project delivery.
·         Build positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
·         Monitor compliance with V/Line standards, policies and procedures.
·         Support the ongoing improvement of processes, procedures and team practices.
·         Maintain accurate records for reporting and invoicing purposes.
Occasional travel is required across the V/Line network.
About you
We're looking for someone who thrives in a collaborative environment, can manage competing priorities and takes pride in delivering high-quality work You'll be proactive and comfortable working with a range of stakeholders, confident seeking information, connecting the dots and helping keep work moving.
Rail experience is welcomed but not essential; we're interested in people who can bring transferable knowledge from engineering, infrastructure, construction, or project environments and apply it in a process-driven and collaborative setting.
Our ideal candidate will possess the following:
·         Experience in an engineering, infrastructure, construction or project environment.
·         Experience in rail systems, track, civil or structures disciplines.
·         Experience applying processes, procedures or compliance requirements.
·         Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
·         The ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
·         Strong written and verbal communication skills.
·         Proven ability to build positive stakeholder relationships.
·         Experience using Microsoft Office applications.
·         A positive attitude, willingness to learn and ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
If your skills or experience don’t exactly match our listed requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and believe in the potential for growth and development.
Why V/Line
In addition to free myki travel, we offer:
- Community impact – Make a genuine difference. Work in a role that connects Victorians, every day.
- Huge potential – We’re transforming, and you can too. Be a change maker, recognised for your contribution and creativity.
- Dynamic environment – V/Line operates in a constantly changing space. Join a fast-paced and exciting organisation.
- Collaborative team – You’ll be part of a broader supportive team. Surround yourself with talented, passionate peers.
- Flexible working – We support flexible working. Work in a way that supports you to thrive in your role.
We are committed to ensuring a comfortable and accessible recruitment experience. If you need any adjustments or have specific accessibility requirements at any stage of the process, please contact our Talent team at TalentSupport@vline.com.au or 1800 800 007 for confidential support.
As an equal opportunity employer, V/Line is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace and network that reflects the communities we serve. We accept and value the contributions of all our employees regardless of gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, age or disability. We are also proud to be endorsed by Work 180 as a great place for women to work, second year in a row.
V/Line are proud to be a part of the Department of Transport & Planning's Yani Bangal Transport and Planning Portfolio First Peoples Careers Strategy 2023-2028. We take this opportunity to welcome and encourage applications from First Peoples. 
At V/Line, safety is our priority. Successful applicants will undergo relevant pre-employment and medical checks to meet our safe working standards. V/Line is also a proud Child Safe employer.
The selection process may include online assessments, video screening, a medical category 3 check and a behavioural interview.
Applications close: 11.59 pm on Wednesday 28 October 2026

candidates.title: Project Engineer
candidates.abstract: These roles are ideal for engineers looking to take the next step in their career while working on a nationally significant project.
bullets: 12+ month Project Specified term contracts
FIFO roster: 10:4 or 14:7
Opportunity to contribute to one of Australia's largest infrastructure program
candidates.content_text:
Project Engineer
About Inland Rail
Inland Rail is a fast freight line that will be delivered in stages to connect Australia while generating regional opportunities during construction and beyond. Inland Rail is eventually planned to span 1,600km connecting Melbourne and Brisbane via regional Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland. 
When complete, Inland Rail will enhance our national freight network and supply chain capabilities, connecting existing freight routes through rail, roads and ports, and supporting Australia's growth. This includes enabling double-stacked trains to access existing ARTC freight network connections to Perth, Adelaide and the East Coast.
Inland Rail Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of ARTC, is building Inland Rail on behalf of the Australian Government. 
 More information relating to the project can be found here: Inland Rail
About the opportunity 
Project Engineer Opportunities | Inland Rail Program (A2I & I2S)
Help Deliver One of Australia's Largest Infrastructure Projects.
Inland Rail is seeking multiple Project Engineers to join our high-performing project delivery teams across the Albury to Illabo (A2I) and Illabo to Stockinbingal (I2S) sections of the program.
These opportunities are available across both Greenfield and Brownfield construction environments, providing exposure to major civil, rail and infrastructure works that will help reshape Australia's freight network.
What We Offer:
- 12+ month Project Specified term contracts
- FIFO roster options: 10 days on / 4 days off or 14 days on / 7 days off (I2S)
- Work on major rail and civil infrastructure projects
- Exposure to Greenfield and Brownfield delivery environments
- Opportunity to contribute to one of Australia's largest infrastructure programs
- Competitive remuneration package and uplift
Reporting to the Project Manager, you will provide engineering support to the Inland Rail Project Management Team and delivery contractors to ensure works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with schedule, quality, cost and risk objectives.
This is a client-side role where you will play a key role supporting construction activities, contractor performance, safety compliance, quality assurance and project reporting across active project sites.
Key Responsibilities:
- Support the safe delivery of construction activities across the Inland Rail project.
- Monitor contractor performance to ensure works are completed safely, on schedule and to the required quality standards.
- Conduct site inspections, audits and quality assurance activities, including hold points, witness points and work lot closeout.
- Review construction schedules, track progress and help resolve delivery challenges.
- Assist with technical reviews, RFIs, design changes and construction documentation.
- Work closely with contractors, supervisors and project stakeholders to coordinate project activities.
- Contribute to project reporting, risk management and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Promote Inland Rail's CARE Values and maintain a strong safety culture across project sites.
About you
 To be successful, you will bring:
- Degree qualification in Civil Engineering.
- Experience on major infrastructure, rail or civil construction projects.
- Experience working in project delivery and construction environments.
- Understanding of quality management, inspections and assurance processes.\
- Understanding of workplace health and safety principles.
- Strong planning, organisation and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to build effective working relationships with contractors and stakeholders.
- Commercial awareness and sound engineering judgement.
- Current Class C Driver's Licence.
What you'll be joining 
- You will join a complex infrastructure project delivering widespread and long-term benefits to Australia, especially regional communities, job seekers and businesses.
- Inland Rail is proud to have over 40% female representation, and we want to encourage more women to join our team. We're proud to be endorsed by WORK180 and be recognised as an employer of choice for women.
- Inland Rail provides an agile working environment in our state-of-the art office embracing flexible working conditions.
Our Organisation and Culture
 The values that drive us and the work we deliver in the program incorporate Collaboration, Accountability, Respect and Excellence. We welcome like-minded individuals who value our culture.
At Inland Rail, we celebrate, support, and thrive on attracting people from all horizons and walks of life for the benefit of our employees, our program, and our community. 
Inland Rail is proud to be an equal opportunity and an affirmative action employer. We encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates to submit their details to us.
All employment is decided based on suitability to the role, cultural fit, merit, and business needs.
Apply Now
If this opportunity sounds like the challenge you have been looking for please apply online today.
As part of the application process, you will be required to undergo pre-employment criminal history, reference and medical checks, including drug and alcohol testing. Inland Rail is a drug and alcohol-free working environment. 
Please note that applications are reviewed from point of advertising so don't delay your application.

candidates.title: Estimator – Commercial Partitions, Ceilings & Fit-Out
candidates.abstract: Join TTC's vibrant team! Estimate commercial partitions, ceilings, glazing, doors and hardware. Experienced estimators and tradespeople welcome.
bullets: Immediate Start
Trusted, long-term role
Stable, supportive workplace
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
What's your expected annual base salary?
How many years' experience do you have as an Estimator?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
candidates.content_text:
Estimator – Commercial Partitions, Ceilings & Fit-Out
Total Trade Constructions | Croydon, Melbourne VIC
Full-Time | Permanent | Salary 
Know your way around steel stud framing, plasterboard, ceilings, doors and hardware, or aluminium systems? Already estimating, or looking to take your experience from the tools into the office?
Total Trade Constructions (TTC) is looking for a motivated Estimator to join our established Commercial Fit-Out division.
We're open to applications from both experienced commercial fit-out estimators and skilled tradespeople looking to transition into an office-based estimating career.
This is an opportunity to work directly with our Managing Director, Head of Commercial Fit-Out and experienced delivery team, pricing projects for some of Melbourne's leading commercial builders.
About TTC
Total Trade Constructions is an established Melbourne commercial subcontractor with dedicated divisions in Commercial Fit-Out and Concreting.
This position sits within our Commercial Fit-Out division, which delivers a wide range of projects across Melbourne, including commercial offices, workplace fit-outs, refurbishments, universities and education facilities.
Our specialist trade packages include:
- Steel stud framing and plasterboard partitions
- Suspended, acoustic and architectural feature ceilings
- Aluminium framing and internal glazed partition systems
- Commercial doors, frames, door hardware and associated installation works
- Commercial carpentry, internal linings and architectural finishes
- Associated commercial interior and fit-out works
We have long-standing relationships with leading Melbourne builders, a strong pipeline of tender opportunities and an experienced team delivering our projects.
We're proud of the culture we've built at TTC. We're a young, motivated and energetic team that enjoys working together, supports one another and takes pride in delivering quality projects. We have a vibrant office environment where everyone is encouraged to contribute ideas, take ownership and enjoy what they do.
The Opportunity
We're looking for someone to take ownership of our estimating and pre-construction workflow, from the moment a tender enquiry comes through to the handover of a successful project to our delivery team.
Working closely with our Managing Director and Head of Commercial Fit-Out, you'll help assess which opportunities we pursue, prepare accurate and competitive quotations and maintain strong communication with our builder clients throughout the tender process.
This is a hands-on, specialist trade-estimating position, not a general building estimator role.
You'll be pricing the work our own teams deliver, with a focus on understanding construction details, quantities, materials, labour, supplier pricing, installation methods and practical buildability.
You'll have the opportunity to take real ownership of your work, build relationships with builders and suppliers, and contribute to the continued development of our estimating systems and processes.
What You'll Be Doing
- Managing incoming tender opportunities and maintaining our CRM and estimating pipeline.
- Reviewing architectural drawings, specifications, schedules and tender documentation.
- Completing detailed quantity take-offs for partitions, ceilings, aluminium, glazing, doors, hardware and associated commercial fit-out works.
- Preparing accurate estimates covering materials, labour, plant, access requirements and project-specific costs.
- Obtaining and reviewing supplier and specialist trade quotations, including maintaining competitive material and trade pricing.
- Building and maintaining relationships with key suppliers, manufacturers and trade partners.
- Identifying scope gaps, discrepancies and risks, and submitting RFIs to builders.
- Preparing and submitting professional tender quotations, including scope qualifications and exclusions.
- Managing tender revisions, repricing, value-management options and alternative construction solutions.
- Liaising with builders, suppliers, manufacturers and our internal delivery teams throughout the tender process.
- Attending site inspections, tender meetings and project walk-throughs when required.
- Supporting builder relationships through professional communication and proactive tender follow-up.
- Preparing clear and accurate project handovers when tenders are successful.
- Helping improve TTC's estimating systems, pricing databases, templates and processes, including the use of AI and modern digital tools.
Who We're Looking For
Ideally, you'll bring experience in commercial partitions, ceilings, plastering, steel stud framing, carpentry, doors and hardware, aluminium systems or a related commercial interiors trade.
We're particularly interested in hearing from:
- Experienced Estimators: Currently working for commercial fit-out contractors or specialist trade subcontractors.
- Commercial Tradespeople: Framing carpenters, plasterers, door installers or aluminium installers with a strong understanding of plans and construction methods.
- Tradespeople Looking for a Change: Someone with a solid commercial trade background, good computer skills and an interest in transitioning from the tools into an estimating career.
- Developing Estimators: Individuals with some estimating experience who are looking to take on greater responsibility and further develop their skills.
You'll be organised, commercially minded and comfortable communicating with builders, suppliers and colleagues.
Strong computer skills and an eye for detail are essential. Experience with digital take-off software, Excel, CRM platforms and AI-assisted workflows would be advantageous.
We're looking for someone with a positive attitude, a willingness to learn and the motivation to become an important part of our team.
Previous estimating experience is highly regarded, but we're prepared to train the right person with a solid commercial trade background and the right attitude.
Why Join TTC?
- Great Team & Culture: Join a young, energetic and motivated team in a fun, vibrant and supportive office environment.
- Established Business: Be part of a respected Melbourne commercial subcontractor with strong builder relationships and consistent tender opportunities.
- Work Alongside Experienced Leaders: Work directly with our Managing Director, Head of Commercial Fit-Out and experienced delivery team.
- Genuine Career Development: Whether you're an experienced estimator or transitioning from the tools, we'll support you in developing your skills and growing with the business.
- Modern Systems & Technology: Join a business actively investing in technology, AI and smarter estimating processes, with opportunities to help shape how we work.
- Interesting Commercial Projects: Work across a variety of commercial offices, workplace fit-outs, refurbishments and education projects throughout Melbourne.
- Ownership & Responsibility: Have the opportunity to manage your own tender workload, contribute ideas and make a genuine impact on the business.
- Competitive Salary: Remuneration tailored to your trade knowledge, estimating capabilities and experience.
Ready for Your Next Move?
Whether you're already an estimator or an experienced commercial tradesperson looking to move off the tools, we'd love to hear from you.
If you understand how commercial interiors are built, enjoy solving problems, have a good attitude and want to work with a motivated team that genuinely enjoys what they do, this could be the opportunity for you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a brief outline of your relevant commercial construction or estimating experience.
Total Trade Constructions – Certainty. Delivered.
candidates.teaser: Join TTC's vibrant team! Estimate commercial partitions, ceilings, glazing, doors and hardware. Experienced estimators and tradespeople welcome.

Residential Scaffold Group is seeking a motivated and experienced Estimator to join our team.
This role is suited to someone with strong attention to detail, good organisational skills and the ability to interpret building plans and project requirements. Experience within estimating, construction or scaffolding will be highly regarded.
Working as part of our estimating team, you will be responsible for preparing accurate and timely estimates and quotations for residential scaffolding projects while working closely with customers, internal staff and management.
 About the Role
As an Estimator, your responsibilities will include:
- Preparing accurate scaffold estimates and quotations
- Reading and interpreting residential building plans and construction drawings
- Assessing project requirements and determining scaffold requirements
- Completing take-offs, measurements and pricing
- Reviewing plans, specifications and job information for accuracy
- Identifying potential issues, exclusions or additional requirements during the estimating process
- Liaising with builders, customers and internal team members where required
- Following up outstanding information required to complete quotations
- Maintaining accurate estimating records and job documentation
- Managing multiple estimates and priorities within required timeframes
- Assisting with variations and revised project requirements where necessary
About You
The successful applicant will ideally have:
- Previous estimating experience within construction, scaffolding or a related industry
- The ability to confidently read and interpret building plans and drawings
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy
- Good numerical and measurement skills
- Strong computer and data-entry skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Strong organisational and time-management skills
- The ability to manage multiple jobs and competing priorities
- Confidence communicating with customers, builders and internal staff
- The ability to work independently while contributing to a team environment
- A practical and solution-focused approach to their work
Previous scaffolding experience would be highly regarded; however, applicants with estimating experience from other areas of residential construction are also encouraged to apply.
For the right applicant with strong construction knowledge and the ability to read plans, additional training in scaffold-specific estimating can be provided.
 What We Offer
- Full-time permanent position
- Competitive salary based on experience
- Ongoing training and support
- Stable employment within a growing company
- Opportunity to further develop your estimating and construction knowledge
- Career progression opportunities
- Supportive and experienced team environment
Your Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity to join an established and growing scaffolding business in a key estimating role.
If you are an experienced estimator, or have a strong background within construction and are looking to develop your estimating career within the scaffolding industry, we would like to hear from you.
 Apply now with your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

Our Geology team at Kal East Gold Mine is expanding and we are looking for recent or graduating Graduate Geologists to join us – we have multiple opportunities in both Underground and Open Pit operations.
