candidates.abstract: Our Grad Program is designed for talented, passionate grads who are looking to join an agile world leader and to use the power of tech to deliver miss
candidates.content_text:
AI & Innovation Full Stack Engineer 
University Internship | Undergraduate Position 
DXC Technology • OASIS Platform • AI & Innovation 
Our Graduate Program is designed for talented, passionate graduates who are looking to join an agile world leader and are ready to use the power of technology to deliver mission-critical IT services that move the world.
About DXC Technology 
DXC Technology (NYSE: DXC) is a leading enterprise technology and innovation partner delivering software, services, and solutions to global enterprises and public sector organizations — helping them harness AI to drive outcomes at a time of exponential change with speed. With deep expertise in Managed Infrastructure Services, Application Modernization, and Industry-Specific Software Solutions, DXC modernizes, secures, and operates some of the world’s most complex technology estates. Learn more on dxc.com
About the Role 
We are looking for a motivated and curious university student to join our AI & Innovation team as a Full Stack Engineer Intern. You do not need to be an expert — we are looking for someone who is enthusiastic about technology, eager to learn, and willing to get hands-on with real problems. 
You will contribute to both frontend and backend work, help build and test prototypes, and get exposure to AI tools and cloud platforms. This is a great opportunity to apply what you have learned at university to industry challenges and build your professional portfolio. 
What You Will Do 
- 
Assist the team in building and testing frontend and backend components for our platform. 
- 
Help create and update technical documentation for projects and features. 
- 
Participate in team meetings, stand-ups, and sprint ceremonies to understand how Agile delivery works in practice. 
- 
Collaborate with engineers, designers, and product owners to understand requirements and contribute ideas. 
- 
Learn about and experiment with AI tools and technologies as part of the AI & Innovation workstream. 
- 
Help troubleshoot basic issues in the application stack and support testing activities. 
- 
Stay curious — explore new frameworks, tools, and technologies as they emerge. 
Eligibility Requirements 
Requirement 
Detail 
Study 
Currently enrolled in a 3-year university degree and have completed at least 2 years of study 
Discipline 
Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field 
Availability 
Able to work full-time depending on study schedule and internship arrangement 
Work Rights 
Must have valid work rights in Australia 
Skills We Are Looking For 
We know you are still studying — you do not need to be an expert in everything below. We just want to see that you have had some exposure and are keen to keep learning. 
Essential Skills 
- 
Basic understanding of frontend development — some experience with HTML, CSS, or JavaScript (even from coursework counts). 
- 
Some exposure to a backend language such as Python or Node.js. 
- 
Familiarity with version control concepts — ideally you have used Git at least once (e.g. for a university project). 
- 
Basic understanding of how databases work and the ability to write simple SQL queries. 
- 
Comfortable using both Windows and/or Linux environments. 
- 
Good written and verbal communication — you can explain what you are working on clearly. 
- 
Curious and willing to learn — technology changes fast and we want someone who enjoys keeping up. 
- 
Able to work as part of a team and ask for help when needed. 
Nice to Have (Bonus, Not Required) 
- 
Any exposure to cloud platforms — AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud (even just knowing what they are). 
- 
Awareness of what Docker or containers are. 
- 
Some interest in or exposure to AI tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, or similar. 
- 
Experience building a project outside of university — a personal project, hackathon entry, or open source contribution. 
- 
Basic understanding of REST APIs (what they are and how they work). 
What You Will Gain 
- 
Real-world experience working on a live enterprise platform used by large organisations. 
- 
Mentoring and guidance from experienced engineers and technical leads. 
- 
Exposure to modern engineering practices including Agile, CI/CD, and cloud-based development. 
- 
A professional reference and, for high-performing interns, potential pathways to graduate or junior roles at DXC. 
- 
Hands-on experience you can add to your resume and portfolio. 
Trust, Transform & Thrive 
DXC Technology’s mission is to lead clients on their digital transformation journeys. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we actively invest in the careers of our people — including the next generation. If you are passionate about technology, eager to learn, and ready to contribute, we would love to hear from you. 
Our Culture and benefits
DXC is committed to building better futures for our customers, colleagues, environment, and communities. We take care of each other and foster a culture of inclusion, belonging and corporate citizenship. We put this to action developing and implementing societal initiatives within our Social Impact Practice. #WeAreDXC
As an employer of choice, our “people first” philosophy means we offer competitive remuneration, benefits, training and career opportunities that reflect our commitment to improving the lives of our employees, and the communities in which we live and work. Some of these include;
- Extensive resources to support your onboarding and continual development including DXC University
- We know that great people refer great people. We will reward you when you bring your friends and family to work at DXC
- More time to do the things you love with flexible leave options, including purchased leave
- Take time to give back with charitable and emergency services volunteer days
- Well-being matters to us and our Employee Assistance Program is there to support you and your family
- And of course, all the basics; novated leasing, discounted health insurance, paid parental leave and many other discounts
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer
DXC is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and we welcome submissions from people from all walks of life. We celebrate our diversity and recognise it is the unique contributions of our people that give us our edge. We stand by the ‘bring your whole-self to work’ philosophy. It is our inclusive culture that powers our results, and our company grows only if our people grow.
Accommodation of special needs for qualified candidates may be considered within the framework of the DXC Accommodation Policy. In addition, DXC Technology is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to support qualified individuals with physical and mental disabilities.
At DXC Technology, we believe strong connections and community are key to our success. Our work model prioritizes in-person collaboration while offering flexibility to support wellbeing, productivity, individual work styles, and life circumstances. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.
Recruitment fraud is a scheme in which fictitious job opportunities are offered to job seekers typically through online services, such as false websites, or through unsolicited emails claiming to be from the company. These emails may request recipients to provide personal information or to make payments as part of their illegitimate recruiting process. DXC does not make offers of employment via social media networks and DXC never asks for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process, nor ask a job seeker to purchase IT or other equipment on our behalf. More information on employment scams is available here.

candidates.content_text:
CPB Contractors is Australia’s leading contractor and the largest infrastructure construction company in our region. Part of the CIMIC Group, we are proud to be constructing Australia’s future and do so collaboratively with our partners and clients.
We hire for careers, not project life. CPB Contractors has more than 50 major infrastructure projects in delivery, across all key sectors of the construction industry, including roads and bridges, rail, tunnelling, defence, airports, buildings and resources, providing you with career opportunities for years to come.
The Project
We are currently seeking an experienced Traffic Engineer to join our project delivery team on a project based in Mackay.
This role offers the opportunity to work on a significant piece of critical infrastructure, supporting the planning, approval, implementation and monitoring of traffic management requirements across multiple active construction work fronts. Due to the linear nature of the project, work locations will be dynamic and will require close coordination with construction teams, traffic management providers, road authorities, stakeholders and local communities.
The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring safe, efficient and compliant traffic management solutions that support project delivery while minimising impacts to road users, residents and businesses.
About the Role
Reporting to the Construction Manager, you will be responsible for coordinating traffic management activities across the project and ensuring all traffic control arrangements are planned, approved, implemented and monitored in accordance with project and regulatory requirements.
Key responsibilities include:
- Planning and coordinating traffic management requirements for multiple construction work fronts.
- Reviewing and managing Traffic Guidance Schemes (TGS), Traffic Management Plans (TMPs) and Traffic Control Permits.
- Liaising with traffic management subcontractors to ensure safe and compliant implementation of traffic control measures.
- Coordinating approvals and permits with local councils, road authorities and relevant stakeholders.
- Monitoring construction activities to ensure compliance with approved traffic management arrangements.
- Supporting project programming by identifying and managing traffic-related constraints and opportunities.
- Managing stakeholder communications relating to traffic impacts, road closures and changed traffic conditions.
- Conducting site inspections, audits and reviews of traffic control arrangements.
- Assisting with incident investigations and implementing corrective actions where required.
- Maintaining project records, approvals, reports and compliance documentation.
- Contributing to project planning, risk management, safety and environmental objectives.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
- Experience managing traffic control and traffic management requirements on civil construction or infrastructure projects.
- Strong understanding of Queensland traffic management requirements, guidelines and approval processes.
- Experience coordinating traffic management subcontractors and field operations.
- Ability to work collaboratively with project engineers, supervisors, subcontractors, road authorities and stakeholders.
- Strong planning, organisational and communication skills.
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities across multiple active work fronts.
- Sound understanding of construction methodologies and project delivery requirements.
- Commitment to safety, quality and environmental compliance.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential:
- Degree qualification in Civil Engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline.
- Minimum 5 years' experience in civil construction, infrastructure delivery or traffic management coordination roles.
- Experience delivering traffic management solutions within live traffic environments.
- Current driver's licence.
Desirable:
- Traffic engineering qualifications or postgraduate studies in traffic and transport engineering.
- Registration or eligibility for registration as a Professional Engineer in Queensland (RPEQ).
- Experience working on water, utilities, pipeline, transport or linear infrastructure projects.
- Traffic Management Designer accreditation or equivalent.
- Experience with TMR, local government and utility authority approval processes.
What We Offer
- Opportunity to work on a major Queensland infrastructure project.
- Diverse and challenging work across multiple construction fronts.
- Supportive project team environment.
- Competitive remuneration package.
- Long-term career development opportunities within a growing organisation.
If you are a proactive and solutions-focused engineer with experience managing traffic requirements in complex construction environments, we would like to hear from you.

There are various rosters across our different works, permanent and casual positions available.

- Strong understanding of project management principles 
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills 
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) 
- A valid Australian Driver’s Licence 
- Proof of right to work in Australia
Life at Monadelphous
There’s lots to get involved in, celebratory or cultural events and so much more. We work hard to make Monadelphous a truly great place to work.
We celebrate our diversity and shared values and are committed to inclusion and equal opportunities for all. We’re committed to hiring locally, encourage people of all diverse backgrounds to apply and strongly encourage women and First Nations people to submit an application.
About us
Monadelphous is an ASX-200 company providing multidisciplinary construction, maintenance and industrial services to many of the largest companies in the resources, energy and infrastructure sectors. Established in 1972, we’ve been working in Australia and around the world for more than 50 years. We work on the biggest projects and ensure our teams have a variety of opportunities available to follow their career path of choice.
Our Maintenance and Industrial Services division specialises in providing comprehensive, multidisciplinary maintenance and improvement solutions for customers across Australia and internationally, through a network of supporting workshops and operations in key regional areas, within the resources, energy and industrial sectors. Our expertise encompasses a wide range of services including the planning, management and execution of mechanical and electrical maintenance and project services, shutdowns, civil and infrastructure works, fixed plant maintenance services, access solutions, specialist coatings and rail maintenance services.
We have been part of the local Mackay community for over 25 years, proud to be providing jobs for the region in the Resources and Mining sector.
Safety is at the forefront of everything we do, and we live by our promise: The Safe Way is the Only Way. Apply now to get started. A career at Monadelphous is a career with a difference. Make it yours.

candidates.content_text:
Modular has had a big year in WA. There's $49 million of government backing, and around half of new social housing builds now use alternative construction methods. Suddenly everyone's an expert. You were pricing it before it was a press release.
 I'm Andrew from Itch. Modular still gets compared to flat-pack furniture. It isn't, but here are your assembly instructions anyway.
 CONTENTS OF THE BOX (what's in it for you)
 - $150K to $190K + super, depending on experience
 - A brand new role. No predecessor, no inherited spreadsheet
 - South of the river, with parking on site
 - Major accommodation camp tenders for some of Australia's biggest miners
 - The real split: 50% commercial manager, 30% technical coordinator, 20% cost engineer
 ASSEMBLY STEPS (the job)
 - Work with the Bids team on RFTs, RFQs and EOIs, and flag the commercial and technical risks
 - Price the whole camp: prelims, materials, trades, foundations, civils, cranage, installation, power, water and wastewater, labour, flights, commissioning and demob
 - Get and compare pricing from civil, electrical and hydraulic contractors, HVAC suppliers, freight providers and crane crews
 - Build the manufacturing, delivery and installation schedules, and know what a slipped date does to the cost
 - Pull engineering, procurement, construction, logistics and HSE together, write the clarifications and departures, and compile the submission
 TOOLS REQUIRED (the must haves)
 - Estimating experience in modular, camp, construction, infrastructure, mining services or EPC
 - Can read drawings, specs and scope, and spot what's missing
 - Comfortable running several big tenders at once
 - Confident with everyone from engineers to subbies
 - Bonus points for PAX calcs, DWER and DoH servicing, remote logistics or camp relocations
 THE HONEST BIT 
Several tenders often run at once, so the deadlines are real. The upside is that your number is the one that counts.
FINAL STEP 
Hit apply with your CV and a line about the biggest camp or modular job you've priced. I'll call you for a confidential chat.
**ONLY APPLICANTS WITH FULL AUSTRALIAN WORKING RIGHTS LIVING IN PERTH WILL BE CONSIDERED**

candidates.title: Environmental Graduate
candidates.abstract: Kick-start your career protecting the land, water and environment behind some of Australia's biggest infrastructure projects.
bullets: Be the first Environmental Graduate with us
Join an established successful graduate program
A genuine career path
candidates.content_text:
Company Description
Nacap is a leading player in the pipeline and civil works industry, and part of the Quanta Services group. We build the infrastructure that supports Australia's energy transition and growing communities — and we believe that building it well means protecting the land, water and cultural heritage around it just as seriously as the build itself. 
Job Description
Kick-start your career protecting the land, water and environment behind some of Australia's biggest infrastructure projects. Nacap is launching a brand-new Environmental Graduate stream — and we're looking for our first intake to start January 2027. 
As an Environmental Graduate, you'll join Nacap's newest Graduate Program stream and get hands-on exposure across every part of how we protect the environment around our projects. Over an 18-month structured program, you'll complete three 6-month rotations: 
- Environmental & Approvals — Implementing the business Environmental Management System (EMS), undertaking approvals and compliance tracking, environmental reporting and providing project environmental support.  
- Site-Based Delivery — two rotations out on a live project site, putting it all into practice through field work, inspections, reporting and day to day environmental management. 
You'll be based at our Doncaster head office for the office-based rotations, with a site-based rotation (FIFO/DIDO) taking you out to where the real work happens. You'll be paired with an experienced mentor, join in-house Masterclasses, and get the support you need to build toward an Environmental Advisor role — and beyond.
Qualifications
We're looking for graduates who are curious, adaptable and genuinely excited about protecting the environment and cultural heritage while infrastructure gets built around them. You'll have: 
- A degree (or be in your final year) in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering or a related discipline. 
- Graduated within the last year, or currently in your final year of study. 
- Strong communication skills, positive approach, and the confidence to build relationships with a huge range of people — Traditional Owners, landholders, regulators and project teams alike. 
- A team-first and proactive attitude, and the willingness to get out on site (FIFO/DIDO) when your rotation calls for it. 
- Previous exposure to environmental management work (an internship, cadetship or site experience) is a bonus, not a requirement — we'll teach you the rest. 
Additional Information
As our first Environmental Graduate, you won't be on the sidelines. You'll have: 
- Real responsibility, early. You'll be trusted with genuine project work from day one, not just observing from the back of the room. 
- A program built around you. Three rotations, a dedicated mentor, in-house Masterclasses and professional development support (including pathways through the Environment Institute of Australia and New Zealand) — all designed to set you up for a long career. 
- A seat at the table. You'll present your experiences directly to Nacap's Operations Leadership Group and Executive Committee — your voice counts here, from year one. 
- A genuine career path. This program is designed to take you from graduate to Environmental Advisor, with plenty of room to keep growing from there. 
- A values-driven culture. Integrity, teamwork and a relentless drive to be better aren't just words on a wall — they shape how we work, every day. 
Perks & benefits 
- Attractive salary package — we value your contribution from day one. 
- Discounts program — everyday savings at over 400 retailers. 
- Employee Assistance Program — support for your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. 
- Generous employee referral program — know a great future teammate? Earn a bonus for the introduction. 
- Flexibility and wellbeing — we understand the importance of balance. 
- Free onsite parking at our Doncaster office. 
- An outstanding, social culture — including volunteer days and a genuinely supportive team. 
How to apply 
This is a rare chance to help shape a brand-new graduate stream at Nacap — and build a career protecting the places we build in. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you. 
To be eligible to apply, you must have Australian or New Zealand citizenship, permanent residency and/or unlimited working rights. Apply now to join our January 2027 intake as our first Environmental Graduate. Be part of the Nacap talent pipeline — and help us build a better tomorrow, responsibly. 
We encourage Aboriginal and or Torres Strait Islanders people to apply.
Please note:  Nacap does not accept any unsolicited resume referrals from Recruitment Agencies. Please do not submit any resumes or associated profiles to any Nacap employees. Should we require additional assistance we will contact our preferred agency partners.
Please note that Nacap does not accept any unsolicited referrals from recruitment agencies, and no recruitment fee is payable without an approved services agreement in place. Please do not submit any resumes or candidate profiles to other employees of Nacap, as all recruitment is managed by the People and Culture team.

candidates.content_text:
Transgrid operates and manages the major high voltage electricity transmission network in NSW and the ACT, connecting generators, distributors and major end users. 
Our core role is to connect electricity consumers to a safe, secure and reliable network through efficient maintenance, proficient operation of assets and prudent investment. Our network is the backbone of the NEM, enabling energy trading between Australia's three largest states along the east coast and supporting the competitive wholesale electricity market
About the role
As part of the Major Projects Development Team, you'll lead the development of major power infrastructure projects from concept through to project definition.
You'll prepare project scopes, engineering concepts, feasibility assessments, support cost estimates and schedules and conduct risk assessments to support investment and approval decisions.
Working closely with planning, design, operations and delivery teams, you'll help deliver practical, cost-effective solutions for substations, transmission lines and network augmentation projects.
This role represents a genuine opportunity to help shape the future of energy infrastructure through meaningful, high-impact project work.
What you'll do
- Lead the development of project scopes, requirements, feasibility studies and option assessments for major transmission infrastructure projects, ensuring alignment with network planning needs and long-term strategic objectives
- Develop concept designs and delivery strategies for substations, transmission lines and reactive plants, ensuring practical, cost-effective and future-ready solutions.
- Facilitate engineering workshops and technical reviews to ensure proposed solutions are practical, constructible and aligned with applicable standards and business requirements
- Provide support in estimating capital cost, scheduling project, conducting risk assessments and preparing business case documentation to facilitate project approvals and successful delivery outcomes.
- Define project staging, delivery strategies and implementation approaches to support efficient execution while minimising network and operational impacts
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders to manage project risks, resolve technical challenges and drive informed decision-making throughout project development.
 What you'll bring
 Tertiary-qualified Electrical Engineer with Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status
- Strong technical knowledge of substation and transmission infrastructures, with proven experience in feasibility assessments, option analysis, concept design development, and project development for large-scale power infrastructure projects.
- Demonstrated ability to develop power project scopes, cost estimates, schedules, business cases and investment proposals that support informed decision-making.
- Proven stakeholder management skills, with the ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams, consultants and external partners to achieve project outcomes.
- Knowledge of project risk management, Australian engineering standards and project delivery frameworks; professional accreditation (CPEng or equivalent) and experience with EHV transmission projects highly regarded.
 Our Values
Transgrid's core values encompass safety, achievement, integrity, and service. Prioritising safety above all, the company emphasises making a meaningful impact through achievement, upholding honesty through integrity, and delivering exceptional outcomes for customers and communities through dedicated service. These values are ingrained in the actions and behaviours of Transgrid's people, who embody them every day.
Benefits & Perks
At Transgrid, we empower our people with a well-rounded benefits package designed to support their personal, professional and social wellbeing, helping them deliver their best work every day.
Transgrid is committed to Health and Safety, the Environment, Equal Employment Opportunity, Diversity and Ethical Practices. All applicants are expected to demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to these areas.
We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and identities, including women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disabilities, culturally and linguistically diverse communities, LGBTQ+ people, mature-age candidates and those returning to the workforce after a career break.
If you require adjustments during any stage of our recruitment process, we're committed to providing support so you can participate fully and perform at your best.
Applications close: Wednesday, 28th October 2026. Please note, our vacancy close dates may be subject to change, we will assess applications as they are received. 
We do not accept agency introductions as Transgrid operates a direct sourcing model.

candidates.content_text:
An exciting opportunity has presented itself to join the Melbourne Metro Field Services team as a Field Engineer working on the nbn network. 
The Field Services (FS) team delivers field workforce capabilities across all nbn technologies, encompassing service activation, network assurance and maintenance, quality inspection activities, and the management of customer complaints associated with network faults.
A bit about your role 
Based in Melbourne, your role as a Field Engineer requires you to represent nbn’s Field Services team across all field‑based assurance activities spanning all nbn network technologies, including FTTx,HFC, Fixed Wireless and Satellite. You will be responsible for support, integration, augmentation, field audits, connect quality, and Delivery Partner quality activities across nbn and the services connected to the network.
You will provide high‑level field support involving travel, scheduled after‑hours activities as part of a dedicated night works roster, participation in an on‑call roster, and responding to after‑hours call‑outs.
This role involves field investigations and network assurance, maintenance, and fault rectification for equipment and systems across all nbn technologies. Responsibilities include the identification, rectification, and maintenance of network issues, providing on‑site technical support, and probing early network faults to ensure ongoing network integrity and performance.
A bit about you  
The ideal candidate would have a technical background, preferably with robust network assurance expertise in one or more nbn technologies like Ethernet, DWDM, GPON, or HFC. Experience in outside plant/inside plant construction across Fibre or HFC networks would be advantageous. This technical proficiency, combined with a strong background in network assurance, would be highly beneficial for this role. 
You will demonstrate strong problem‑solving skills with a disciplined and methodical approach. The role requires the ability to learn rapidly, remain flexible, and manage conflicting priorities. You will be a highly organised team player who can adapt to a changing and dynamic work environment.
Life at nbn
To be part of nbn is to be part of something bigger. There’s so much more from here. Our pioneering spirit drives us forward every day. Together, we help lift the digital capability of the nation by building and connecting Australia’s best fibre infrastructure into homes and businesses, plus places and things, everywhere. We’re continuing to create Australia’s network—a network made for more. Not just a way for everyone to do the things they love but transforming the way they do them.
A more inclusive working world
nbn is committed to an inclusive, flexible, and supportive workplace where everyone can feel heard, valued, and respected. We believe diverse perspectives are the key to unlocking greater outcomes and encourage applications from people of all ages, nationalities, abilities, and cultures. That's why we have a Reconciliation Action Plan, Accessibility & Inclusion Plan, offer 18 weeks of paid parental leave, are a Pride in Diversity Platinum Employer, and have active employee-led diversity pillars. Click here to see our list of employee benefits and why we're recognised as a WORK180 Endorsed Employer for Women.
Equal Opportunities for All
We champion equal opportunities for all employees. If you have any accessibility requirements and would like to discuss adjustments for the recruitment process, please don’t hesitate to contact us by emailing recruitment@nbnco.com.au or calling our Recruitment Accessibility Enquiry Line at +61 2 8918 9990. Please note, this line is dedicated to accessibility-related enquiries for the purposes of recruitment, and only enquiries related to accessibility adjustments will be answered. For other matters, please visit our Contact Us page on our website.
Where to from here?
If you think this role might be for you, we want to hear from you. Please apply by following the links and send your resume only.  We do not require a cover letter or any selection criteria to be addressed.
Please note that this role is a Permanent opportunity and applications will close at midnight on 28 October 2026.
To be eligible for this role, you must have full working rights in Australia.

EnergyCo NSW is helping shape the state’s energy future by coordinating the planning and delivery of infrastructure to support the transition to a reliable, affordable and renewable electricity system.
About the Opportunity
Join EnergyCo and play a key role in supporting the delivery of NSW’s renewable energy future. As a Power System Analysis Engineer, you will undertake power system modelling and analysis that supports the successful integration of Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) infrastructure, helping to deliver a secure, reliable and sustainable electricity network. Working alongside experienced engineers, industry stakeholders and government partners, you will contribute to major infrastructure projects, provide technical insights, and help develop innovative solutions that support the state's energy transformation.
About You
You are an engineer with experience in power system planning, modelling or analysis and a genuine interest in renewable energy integration. Ideally, you will be able to hit the ground running, bringing practical experience with power system studies and a solid understanding of the electricity network. However, we are equally interested in candidates who have strong foundational technical skills and are ready to take the next step in their career within a supportive and high-performing team.
You are proactive, curious and motivated to learn, with a willingness to tackle complex technical challenges and contribute to meaningful infrastructure outcomes. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills will help you build effective working relationships across industry, government and project teams, while your collaborative approach and focus on delivering quality outcomes will enable you to thrive in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
Essential Requirements
- Degree in electrical engineering or equivalent relevant experience.
For more information read the full Role Description: Power System Analysis Engineer
Who we are?
The Energy Corporation of NSW (EnergyCo) is a statutory corporation established under the Energy and Utilities Administration Act 1987 and governed by its Board, appointed by the Minister for Energy.  EnergyCo is a Staff Agency employing all EnergyCo staff and is an agency related to the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW).
EnergyCo plays a pivotal role in the NSW Government’s Electricity Infrastructure Roadmap, which aims to transform the state’s electricity system into one that is cheap, clean, and reliable. As Infrastructure Planner under the Electricity Infrastructure Investment Act 2020, EnergyCo is responsible for leading the delivery of the State’s first five Renewable Energy Zones (REZs) and the first two priority network infrastructure projects (PTIPs), which are located in the Central-West Orana, New England, South West, Hunter-Central Coast, and Illawarra regions. We work closely with communities, investors, and industry to investigate, plan, recommend and coordinate generation, storage and network infrastructure projects.
We acknowledge the ongoing custodial responsibilities of the Aboriginal peoples of NSW to care for Country and water and are committed to establishing meaningful partnerships with Aboriginal peoples in the management of the environment.

candidates.content_text:
ARL Laboratory Services Pty Ltd is seeking a qualified and motivated Materials Engineer to join our team in Sydney, NSW. The successful candidate will be responsible for conducting material testing, metallurgical investigations, mechanical evaluations, and failure analysis to ensure the quality, integrity, and performance of a wide range of materials.
The ideal candidate will possess strong technical knowledge, practical laboratory experience, analytical skills, and the ability to deliver accurate and reliable results in a professional laboratory environment.
Key Responsibilities:
- Conduct metallographic examinations and microstructural studies of various materials.
- Perform structural, mechanical, and metrological evaluations in accordance with applicable standards and testing procedures.
- Conduct chemical analysis and material characterization of metals, polymers, composites, and other engineering materials.
- Operate and maintain laboratory testing equipment, including tensile testing machines, hardness testers, Charpy impact testers, and universal testing machines (UTMs).
- Perform tensile, compression, strength, shear, impact, and load testing.
- Conduct hardness testing using Vickers, Brinell, and Rockwell hardness testing equipment.
- Perform macrostructural and microstructural examinations of materials, including welded components and structures.
- Utilize material characterization techniques, including Positive Material Identification (PMI), Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX/EDS), and optical microscopy.
- Conduct material inspections and assessments of tanks, welded structures, and other engineering components using appropriate testing and characterization techniques.
- Investigate material failures and determine the potential causes of failure in welded structures and other engineering components.
- Carry out destructive and non-destructive testing (NDT) of metallic components and structures that have been in service.
- Evaluate material properties and recommend suitable materials based on application requirements, service conditions, and relevant engineering specifications.
- Perform quality control inspections and material verification to ensure compliance with applicable standards and customer requirements.
- Contribute to the planning, execution, and evaluation of laboratory studies and experimental investigations.
- Analyze test results, interpret technical data, and prepare comprehensive technical reports in collaboration with other team members.
- Liaise with clients to clarify technical requirements, discuss testing procedures, and ensure accurate results and a high level of customer satisfaction.
- Maintain accurate laboratory records and ensure testing activities comply with established quality procedures and safety requirements.
General Requirements and Qualifications:
- Diploma or degree in Materials Engineering, Metallurgy, Materials Science, or a related engineering discipline.
- A minimum of three years of practical experience in product testing or materials testing within a laboratory environment is preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in metallography, microstructural analysis, and material characterization.
- Practical experience with tensile, compression, and strength testing equipment, including Instron, MTS, or equivalent universal testing machines.
- Experience operating mechanical testing equipment, including hardness and impact testing machines.
- Practical machining skills, including the operation of milling machines, lathes, and related equipment, will be highly regarded.
- Sound understanding of engineering principles, including mechanical systems, testing fixtures, tooling, and material behavior.
- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex technical data.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare technical reports and communicate effectively with clients and colleagues.
- Strong organizational skills and a high level of attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and perform effectively in a dynamic and changing work environment.
- A professional attitude, commitment to quality, and a customer-focused approach to laboratory services.
Preferred Technical Expertise:
Experience in the following areas will be highly regarded:
- Metallurgical testing and failure analysis.
- Chemical composition analysis and material verification.
- Macro- and microstructural examination of welds and metallic components.

candidates.content_text:
Do you see opportunity everywhere in anywhere connectivity? Then come and propel your career at Myriota, where the Internet of Things (IoT) meets Space!
At Myriota our mission is audacious yet simple: unlock better outcomes for people and planet, through simple, affordable access to data. We make anywhere connectivity possible through our patented direct-to-satellite technology that is secure, low-cost, low maintenance and really (really) long-battery-life.
One more thing… It works today. This is why our solutions are profitably unlocking vital use cases across a range of industries including agriculture, environmental monitoring, transport, logistics, maritime and defence.
The incredible opportunity:
As an NPI (New Product Introduction) Engineer within our Edge team, you will act as the primary technical anchor taking complex, satellite-connected electronic hardware from R&D prototype into scaled, commercial contract manufacturing.
Reporting directly to the Electronics Lead, you will bridge the gap between engineering design and high-volume mass production. You’ll embed Design for Manufacture (DFM) and Design for Test (DFT) early in the design cycle, architect automated production test fixtures, drive factory quality frameworks, and collaborate with both local and offshore Contract Manufacturers (CMs) to ensure our direct-to-orbit edge hardware is delivered reliably, cost-effectively, and at scale.
What we’ll trust you with: 
- Leading the end-to-end technical handover of edge hardware from internal R&D to contract manufacturing partners, orchestrating prototype, pilot, and full production build gates.
- Partnering with electronics engineers early in development to evaluate schematics, PCB layouts, assembly tolerances, and component selection to maximize first-pass yield (FPY).
- Specifying, designing, and rolling out automated factory test fixtures, test software, and assembly processes that ensure 100% functional test coverage prior to deployment.
- Directing day-to-day technical engagement with local and remote CMs, defining SOPs, standard process flows, and rapidly resolving production-floor technical inquiries.
- Driving root-cause investigations on manufacturing defects using structured quality methodologies, including PFMEA, 8D analysis, and Pareto tracking to systematically eliminate scrap and line failures.
- Maintaining engineering change orders (ECOs), ensuring design integrity, and verifying requirements against strict Verification & Validation (V&V) traceability matrices.
- Leaning in with an "all hands on deck" mindset to support ad-hoc engineering challenges, alternative component sourcing, and cross-functional hardware priorities as we grow.
What we'd love to see in you: 
- Bachelor’s degree in Electronics Engineering, Mechatronics, Process Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
- 3+ years of commercial hardware experience transitioning complex electronic products into scaled mass production.
- Hands-on experience working with both local and offshore/remote Contract Manufacturers (CMs) across trial builds and volume ramps.
- Demonstrated ability to specify, build, or implement automated manufacturing test fixtures and test regimes for electronic assemblies.
- Practical experience applying PFMEA, 8D problem solving, yield analysis, and V&V requirements traceability.
- Strong technical documentation skills with the ability to translate complex engineering constraints into clear assembly and test instructions.
- Familiarity with reviewing schematics/PCBs in CAD tools (such as Altium Designer), or exposure to embedded software (C/C++) and scripting (Python, Bash) for test automation and telemetry analysis.
- An analytical, proactive problem solver who is quality-obsessed, self-reliant, and driven by collective team success.
Why Myriota stands out:
- Driven by Purpose: Our mission creates meaningful impacts for both individuals and the planet.
- Shared Values: We embrace values that include Thinking Big, Simplifying, Collaborating, and Staying Authentic.
- Nurturing Growth: Count on tailored development plans that empower your potential. 
- Flexibility & Empowerment: We champion work-life balance, well-being, learning, and individual passions. 
- Caring Community: Our supportive culture offers mental health support, paid parental leave, birthday leave, and comprehensive health coverage. 
Our hiring commitment:
At Myriota, you don’t need to check every box.
We have key requirements which are important, but we also know that the best candidate may not tick all the boxes so, if you have the experience and capabilities for a portion of the role, Apply Now to join our energised team.
At Myriota, we're a diverse team united by strength. We warmly welcome applications from all backgrounds and walks of life. Elevate the future with us at Myriota today!

We love hearing from candidates directly! Please note that Myriota has not engaged any external agencies for this role, and we are managing this recruitment process internally. We kindly ask that recruitment agencies respect this and refrain from cold outreach or submitting unsolicited resumes.

candidates.content_text:
ACCIONA is a global company, leading in the development of regenerative infrastructure that creates a positive impact on society. Our workforce consists of more than 65,000 professionals, present in more than 40 countries across the five continents, all contributing to our mission to design a better planet. Are you a passionate individual who wants to make a difference, promote sustainable development, and find solutions to the biggest global challenges, including climate change, overpopulation, and water scarcity? Come and join us in building the infrastructure our planet needs to achieve a sustainable future.
ACEREZ, a partnership of ACCIONA, COBRA and Endeavour Energy, has been appointed network operator by EnergyCo to design, build, finance, operate and maintain the Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) transmission network. The ACCIONA COBRA Joint Venture (ACJV), the design and construct (D&C) consortium, will design and build the Central-West Orana REZ transmission project.
The Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) Transmission Project will build new high-capacity transmission lines, energy hubs and supporting infrastructure to transfer power generated by solar and wind projects to electricity consumers. The new infrastructure is expected to be operational by 2028 and will initially unlock up to 4.5 gigawatts of new network capacity.
The project consists of 90km of 500kV overhead transmission lines and 150 km of 330kV transmission lines for generator connections, stretching from Elong Elong in the west through to Barigan Creek in the east, via an energy hub at Merotherie.
The Central-West Orana project is currently seeking a dedicated Site Engineer - Civil to share their expertise within our growing Energy Hubs and Substations Teams.
Key Responsibilities
- Ensure all quality and environmental aspects of the project are addressed to maintain effective operation and project delivery.
- Ensures non-conformances are recorded and corrective actions initiated as soon as practically possible.
- Completes all outstanding defects as required by the program.
- Prepares Inspection Test Reports and checklists that accurately reflect contract requirements.
- Provide support on planning the use of materials, resources, components or systems within the project, and construction practices and problems to ensure project success, value for money and best practice are achieved.
- Assist the Project Engineer with development of construction planning documents and monitor implementation.
- Maintain project schedule by monitoring project progress and coordinating activities.
- Assist with preparing project status reports and change orders.
- Assesses progress daily and prepares plan of works for daily cost planning meeting (if held)
- Responsible and accountable to ensure that the requirements of the Contract are being satisfied at work crew level.
- Coordinate resource allocation with the expectation that you would encourage effective teamwork and foster a positive attitude toward the achievement of organisational objectives.
- Tracks subcontractor resources daily and record accurately
- Prepares cost plan/resources for daily cost planning meeting.
Required Skills and Competencies
- Bachelor's degree (Engineering) Civil or Relevant Tertiary Education
- Experience constructing outdoor air insulated substations and substations at 220kV or above
- Tier 1 Contractor experience is preferred, on large scale projects
- Preferable 1 to 3 years post graduate experience in a construction / engineering environment
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with others.
- Establish and steward overall delivery work plans.
- Ensuring all relevant regulatory requirements are satisfied.
- Competent in planning and organising work schedules.
- Working knowledge of HS&E requirements and implementation of same
- Clear communication - verbal and written
Site Engineer positions are bus in bus out, in camp style accommodation provided for 14 days onsite and 7 days off site, on a roster-based arrangement out of the Central West Orana Region, Merotherie.
This position is being delivered as part of a joint venture between two organisations. As such, your employment may be with either of the parent companies, and this will be confirmed during the recruitment process.
We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. If you believe you bring the capabilities to succeed in this role, we'd love to hear from you. We look forward to continuing to build our supportive workplace together.
For more information on how your personal data is managed, please refer to the privacy statements of each parent company:
Grupo Cobra: https://www.grupocobra.com/en/privacy-policy/
Acciona: Privacy Policy | ACCIONA | Business as unusual

About the role
Duffy Kennedy Constructions (DKC) is seeking an experienced and motivated Civil Engineering Draftsperson to join our team in Miranda, NSW. This full-time position plays an important role in supporting our ongoing construction projects by preparing accurate technical drawings, coordinating design documentation, and providing timely drafting support to project managers and site teams. The successful candidate will work closely with our design and construction teams, contributing to the efficient delivery of residential, commercial and other building projects.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare and amend detailed civil and structural engineering drawings using AutoCAD, Revit or other relevant drafting software.

- Liaise with engineers, estimators, project managers and subcontractors to ensure drawings meet project requirements and relevant Australian Standards.

- Relevant tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, Engineering Drafting, Architectural Engineering or a related discipline.
- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in civil or structural engineering drafting, preferably within the building construction industry.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD, Revit or similar drafting software.
- Sound understanding of civil and structural engineering principles, construction methods and technical drawing standards.
- Experience preparing detailed drawings for residential, commercial or multi-storey building projects will be highly regarded.
- Strong attention to detail, problem-solving abilities and organisational skills.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with engineers, project managers and construction personnel.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and respond efficiently to changing project requirements.
Benefits
- Competitive salary package commensurate with qualifications and experience.
- Full-time employment with an established construction company.
- Opportunities to work on a diverse range of residential and commercial construction projects.
- A collaborative working environment with experienced construction professionals.
- Opportunities for ongoing professional development and career progression.
About us
Duffy Kennedy Constructions is an established Sydney-based construction company delivering a diverse range of residential, commercial and other building projects. With extensive experience in the construction industry, we are committed to delivering high-quality projects through effective project management, technical expertise and close collaboration between our office and on-site teams. As our construction activities continue to develop, we are strengthening our internal technical capabilities to support efficient project delivery and maintain high standards across our operations.

candidates.content_text:
Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting! 
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career? 
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry. 
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Structural Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland. 
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn. 
Why you’ll love working here 
Start building your career   Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical Structural drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters. 
Work on real projects   Go beyond the classroom and see how structural engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery. 
Learn from experienced people   Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow. 
Be part of a great team   Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do. 
Work in Fortitude Valley   Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity  
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to: 
- Assist with preparing structural drawings, plans and project documentation. 
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings. 
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes. 
- Develop your understanding of how structural engineering projects are designed and delivered. 
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements. 
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members. 
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop. 
About you: 
You could be a great fit if you are: 
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver, or currently studying Residential Drafting, or an equivalent qualification at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in structural drafting, design and engineering. 
- Curious and keen to learn new skills. 
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work. 
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback. 
- Reliable, organised and willing to have a go at new challenges. 
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team. 
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident. 
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career. 
What’s in it for you? 
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development. 
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution. 
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs. 
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events. 
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program. 
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy. 
About STP Consultants  
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. 
We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take. 
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other. 
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes. 
Ready to get started?   
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you. 
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter. 
In your cover letter, tell us: 
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in structural drafting.   
2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants. 
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.
candidates.teaser: Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career?

candidates.content_text:
At Geosurv, we're proud to be one of NSW's leading surveying and utility businesses, delivering some of the state's largest infrastructure, construction and development projects.
We are looking for an experienced Survey Drafter to join our growing team. If you are passionate about producing high-quality technical drawings, enjoy variety in your work and want to be part of a collaborative business that genuinely invests in its people, we would love to hear from you.
Working alongside our Surveyors, Utility Teams and Project Managers, you will deliver accurate drafting solutions across surveying and utility projects while helping maintain the high standards our clients have come to expect.
The Opportunity
This is a diverse role where you'll work on a wide range of projects, producing accurate survey drawings and technical drafting deliverables that support complex infrastructure, construction and development projects. You will play a key role in delivering quality outcomes while working across multiple disciplines and project types.
You will collaborate with experienced professionals across the business, manage multiple projects simultaneously and play an important role in ensuring deliverables are completed accurately, on time and within budget.
What You Will Be Doing
- Producing high-quality survey drawings and utility drafting deliverables
- Preparing as-built plans, set-out plans, WAE plans, utility plans, detail surveys, heat maps and volume calculations
- Drafting underground utility networks and service information to support utility locating, mapping and asset investigation projects
- Producing cadastral drawings where required
- Completing 12d reductions to support Surveyors across multiple disciplines
- Assisting with BIM and Revit modelling projects
- Reviewing project scopes and ensuring drawings meet client requirements
- Working closely with Surveyors, Utility Teams, Project Managers and clients throughout the project lifecycle
- Managing multiple projects while meeting deadlines and maintaining exceptional quality
- Providing technical guidance and mentoring to junior team members
- Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives across the drafting team
About You
You will be an experienced Survey Drafter who enjoys working in a collaborative environment and takes pride in delivering accurate, high-quality work.
You will also bring:
- A Diploma in Surveying or higher
- At least 5 years' experience in a Survey Drafter role
- Advanced AutoCAD, Civil 3D and 12d skills
- Experience producing surveying and/or utility drafting deliverables
- Strong understanding of surveying principles and drafting standards
- Excellent communication and organisational skills
- The ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines
- A proactive attitude with a strong focus on quality and client service
- White Card
Why Geosurv?
At Geosurv, we know our people are what set us apart. We invest heavily in our team, provide opportunities for career progression and encourage continuous learning and development.
When you join Geosurv, you will enjoy:
- Working on some of NSW's largest infrastructure and construction projects
- A supportive, collaborative and down-to-earth team culture
- Genuine long-term career progression opportunities
- Exposure to a diverse range of surveying and utility projects
- Ongoing training and professional development
- Modern technology and industry-leading software
- A stable, growing business with an outstanding reputation across the industry
If you are looking for your next challenge with a company that values quality, teamwork and technical excellence, we would love to hear from you.
Apply now for a confidential discussion.

candidates.content_text:
Graduate Engineering Officer (Ref: 1348)
About the position:
This position provides engineering support across the Infrastructure Services department with a focus on engineering investigations, roads in compliance with MRWA guidelines to regional road network and asset management, capital works, and asset creation proposals, including funding applications.  The role will also assist with civil design, drafting and estimating, and sustainability and environment initiatives.
Key accountabilities:
- Provide technical and engineering support to the Infrastructure Services department, under the general guidance of the Principal Engineer and Coordinator Design.
- Assist in the assessment of town planning and building applications (including structure plans, subdivisions, stormwater management plans and strategies, and road use assessments), preparing draft comments and conditions notes on behalf of Infrastructure Services Department to be reviewed by an Engineering Officer.
- Process development engineering applications (including crossover installations, bond administration and compliance matters) in accordance with the relevant legal provisions and the City’s Land Development Specifications, developing knowledge of the approvals process.
- Undertake site inspections and engineering investigations in response to requests, complaints and queries on Infrastructure Services related matters, and prepare accurate records, reports and recommendations.
For further information and to view the position description, visit www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/.
To gain a better understanding of the role or to discuss the position qualification requirements in detail, please call Chris Edwards, Manager Project Delivery and Engineering on (08) 9956 6949.
Position requirements:
The successful applicant will ideally hold a Degree in Civil Engineering or Design or progressing towards a Degree. Applicants with significant experience in the design and preparation of civil drawings in 12D and/or AutoCAD including project cost estimating will also be considered.
Completion of a pre-employment medical including alcohol and other substances testing is required of all positions at the City.
Remuneration and benefits:
This position offers a salary starting from $92,692 per annum, commensurate with the successful applicant’s knowledge, skills, experience and qualifications.
Some of the additional benefits of working for the City include:
- Up to 21% Superannuation (with superannuation co-contribution scheme)
- 22 Annual Leave days per annum
- Health & Wellbeing Program
- Flexible working arrangements
- Career opportunities
- Study Assistance
- Centrally located
- Free parking
About the City
Overlooking the Indian Ocean, Geraldton is a thriving regional city at the heart of Australia's Coral Coast. With a growing population of over 41,000 people it offers a wide range of services and activities. Geraldton is recognised as one of WA's key growth areas and the opportunities in this regional city are plentiful. You can be part of working with us to deliver the best for our community and this region.
The City of Greater Geraldton actively welcomes, includes and values the unique contributions of all people in its workplace. The City welcomes applications from all age groups, people with a disability, and those from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer with strong commitment to fitness for work and safety in the workplace.
Interested in applying?
Visit the City’s website: www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/ to apply for this position.
To be considered for this vacancy, applicants are advised to include the following:
- A current resume
- A written response (maximum 1250 characters per criteria) addressing the following selection criteria inclusive of examples to support your claims:
i. Experience in investigations and the preparation of engineering planning reports
ii. Sound understanding of civil engineering principles and practices, with a developing knowledge of development engineering, subdivision and infrastructure assets
iii. Developing knowledge and appreciation of relevant legislation, regulations, Australian Standards, Austroads and Main Roads WA guidelines, and current development engineering requirements within Western Australia (including IPWEA subdivision guidelines)
iv. Sound written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear reports and correspondence and to liaise with interna and external stakeholders
v. Excellent time management skills with ability to organise workloads, meet deadlines and maintain high levels
vi. Ability to use relevant engineering, drafting, MS Office applications and spatial software or a demonstrated aptitude to learn
Applications close 4pm Thursday 15 October 2026.
Ross McKim
CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

The City of Canada Bay is a thriving, colourful community, surrounded by the beautiful bays of Sydney Harbour. The area is also known for its parklands, cycle paths and walkways. City of Canada Bay Council’s values underpin how we operate: 
We act with integrity| We empower our people| We are respectful| We work together| We innovate.
Help shape the infrastructure that supports our community
We are seeking an enthusiastic and capable Infrastructure Engineer to join our team and contribute to the planning, design and delivery of infrastructure projects that support our growing community.
This is an opportunity to apply your engineering expertise across a diverse range of infrastructure projects, from initial investigations and design through to construction, project delivery and contract management.
About the Role
You will assist with the development and delivery of infrastructure engineering projects, preparing designs, project plans, cost estimates, engineering specifications and tender documentation.
You will work across both operational and capital works, undertaking site investigations, inspections and project reviews, while providing practical engineering advice and recommendations to support quality project outcomes.
Key Responsibilities:
 - Assist with the planning, design and delivery of infrastructure projects.
 - Conduct site investigations and inspections and provide recommendations to address infrastructure issues.
 - Prepare project plans, engineering designs, specifications, cost estimates and tender documentation.
 - Monitor project works to ensure compliance with approved scope, specifications and objectives.
 - Support contract management and project administration.
 - Prepare reports, correspondence, grant submissions and other project documentation.
 - Assist with environmental assessments and obtaining relevant project approvals.
 - Provide professional and responsive service to internal stakeholders, contractors and the community.
 - Identify opportunities to improve project delivery, operational efficiency and service outcomes.
 - Promote Council’s work health and safety, risk management and environmental responsibilities.
 - Provide informed engineering recommendations based on project investigations and technical information.
About you
To be successful in this position, you will ideally have the following:
 - Currently undertaking, or recently completed, a tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, or Project Management
 - Demonstrated project and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and Outlook, as well as relevant project management, database and design/drafting software such as AutoCAD.
 - A current Class C Driver Licence.
What’s on offer
We are offering a remuneration between $79,533 to $91,463 per annum plus Super.
The City of Canada Bay also offers excellent employee benefits which include:
 - A range of flexible work arrangements including hybrid work from home arrangements
 - A supportive, energetic, and passionate team
 - Significant leave benefits (sick/personal leave, health and wellbeing leave, access to Long Service leave after 5 years)
 - Continuous training, support, and leadership development
 - Health and Wellbeing programs (Yoga classes, Fitness Passport, Flu vaccinations, Skin Cancer Checks)
 - And much, much more!
Want to know more?
Further information regarding the requirements of this role can be found in the attached Position Description, alternatively for a confidential discussion please contact Vincenzo Camuglia, Coordinator, Infrastructure Design on 02 9911 6287 or email Vincenzo.Camuglia@canadabay.nsw.gov.au 
How to apply
Candidates MUST apply online. Applications close 11:30pm, Thursday 22 October 2026 and will not be accepted through any other medium.
If you have any accessibility requirements, please feel free to contact Grace Aberin on 02 9121 0238  or email  grace.aberin@canadabay.nsw.gov.au   to discuss.
The City of Canada Bay Council is a Child Safe Organisation that recognises and advocates for the rights of Children and Young People and are committed to a Safe Workplace.
The City of Canada Bay Council is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer committed to maintaining, growing and supporting a diverse, respectful, collaborative & inclusive workplace. We welcome and encourage applications from diverse community groups and ages including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, LGBTIQA+, people with disabilities, and other diversity groups.
 Formal offers of employment are subject to standard Council pre-employment checks including medical and other background checks.

GRADUATE / JUNIOR ESTIMATOR – COMMERCIAL CONSTRUCTION
Cairns, QLD | Full-Time | Graduate / Entry Level
WIP Construction is looking for a motivated Graduate or Junior Estimator to join our Cairns-based team. This is an office-based position located in Cairns, Queensland. Applicants must be based in Cairns or willing to relocate.
This is an opportunity for someone who wants to build a career in commercial construction estimating. You don't need previous experience as an Estimator, we're more interested in finding someone with the right aptitude, attitude and genuine desire to learn.
You may be a recent graduate, currently studying, or at the beginning of your construction career and looking for an opportunity to develop practical, hands-on experience within an established commercial construction company.
The Role
Working alongside our experienced estimating and project team, you'll learn how commercial construction projects are priced, tendered and ultimately delivered.
As your experience develops, you'll be involved in:
- Reviewing construction drawings, specifications and tender documentation
- Assisting with quantity take-offs and pricing
- Preparing and issuing subcontractor and supplier enquiries
- Reviewing and comparing quotations
- Assisting with tender submissions
- Understanding project scope, methodology and construction requirements
- Building relationships with subcontractors and suppliers
- Working with our project delivery team to understand how estimates translate into live projects
- Developing your knowledge of commercial construction costs, trades and procurement
We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. We'll teach you.
What we do expect is that you genuinely want to learn.
We're looking for someone who is curious, switched-on and interested in understanding how and why things are built and what they cost.
You may be studying or have recently completed a qualification in:
- Construction Management
- Quantity Surveying
- Civil Engineering
- Building & Construction
- Project Management
- Engineering
- Or another relevant construction-related discipline
We're also open to applicants from other backgrounds who can demonstrate strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in pursuing a career in construction estimating.
Previous estimating experience is not required.
More important to us is someone who:
- Has strong numerical and analytical skills
- Has excellent attention to detail
- Can read information carefully and ask questions when something doesn't make sense
- Is organised and able to manage competing priorities
- Communicates confidently and professionally
- Takes ownership of their work
- Has a genuine interest in building a long-term career in commercial construction
WIP Construction is an established Cairns-based commercial construction company delivering projects throughout Cairns and Far North Queensland.
You'll be joining a team where you'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced construction professionals and gain exposure to real commercial projects from tender through to delivery.
This isn't a graduate role where you'll spend months watching from the sidelines.
You'll be given real work, real responsibility and plenty of support while you develop your skills.
For the right person, there is significant opportunity to grow within the business and develop into an experienced Estimator.
If you're motivated, good with numbers, interested in construction and looking for somewhere to start your career, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, what you're currently studying or have completed, and why estimating and commercial construction interests you.
